title.zh: 卷七十八 宦者列傳
title.raw: 卷七十八 宦者列傳 Volume 78: Biographies of Eunuchs

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：“天垂象，聖人則之。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth its images; the sage takes them as his pattern."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays its signs, and the sage patterns himself upon them."

sentences.zh: ”宦者四星，在皇位之侧，故《周礼》置官，亦备其数。

translations.literal: The four "chamberlain" stars stand beside the throne star; therefore the Rites of Zhou established offices and likewise matched their number.
translations.idiomatic: The four chamberlain stars lie beside the celestial throne, so the Rites of Zhou created offices and filled their quota accordingly.

sentences.zh: 阍者守中門之禁，寺人掌女宫之戒。

translations.literal: Gatekeepers guarded the prohibitions at the inner gates; palace stewards enforced discipline in the women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers watched the inner gates; palace stewards handled security and rules within the women's palace.

sentences.zh: 又云“王之正内者五人”。

translations.literal: It also says, "There are five who attend the ruler's proper inner quarters."
translations.idiomatic: The text also speaks of "five attendants for the ruler's inner household."

sentences.zh: 《月令》：“仲冬，命阉尹审門闾，谨房室。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances: "In midwinter, order the chief eunuch to inspect the gates and lanes and tighten security in the chambers."
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say that in midwinter the chief eunuch must inspect gates and alleys and keep bedchambers secure.

sentences.zh: ”《詩》之《小雅》，亦有《巷伯》刺谗之篇。

translations.literal: In the Minor Odes of the Book of Songs there is also the piece "The Lane Porter," which satirizes slander.
translations.idiomatic: The Minor Odes likewise include "The Lane Porter," a poem that lampoons slander.

sentences.zh: 然宦人之在王朝者，其來旧矣。

translations.literal: Yet for eunuchs who serve in royal courts, their origins lie far in the past.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eunuchs at royal courts trace back to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 将以其体非全气，情志专良，通关中人，易以役养乎？

translations.literal: Is it because their bodies lack intact vital essence, their devotion is single-minded, they move freely among palace insiders, and are therefore easy to employ and maintain?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps because they lack intact vital essence yet remain steadfast, pass easily among those inside the palace, and are simple to command and keep?

sentences.zh: 然而后世因之，才任稍广，其能者，則勃貂、管苏有功于楚、晋，景监、缪贤著庸于秦、趙。

translations.literal: Yet later ages continued the practice, and duties gradually widened; among the capable, Bo Diao and Guan Su served Chu and Jin with merit, Jing Jian and Miao Xian achieved distinction in Qin and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties expanded the role: able men such as Bo Diao and Guan Su aided Chu and Jin, while Jing Jian and Miao Xian won fame in Qin and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及其敝也，則竖刁乱齐，伊戾祸宋。

translations.literal: When it decayed, Shu Diao threw Qi into turmoil and Yi Li brought disaster upon Song.
translations.idiomatic: In decline it produced Shu Diao's chaos in Qi and Yi Li's ruin for Song.

sentences.zh: 汉兴，仍袭秦制，置中常侍官。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it retained Qin institutions and established the office of regular palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han the court kept Qin practice and instituted regular palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 然亦引用士人，以参其选，皆银珰左貂，给事殿省。

translations.literal: Yet it also recruited gentlemen to join the selection; all wore silver pendants and left-side marten tails and served in the palace bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Educated men were also admitted to the corps, bearing silver seals and left martens while staffing the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 及高后称制，乃以張卿为大谒者，出入卧内，受宣詔命。

translations.literal: When Empress Lü exercised regency, she made Zhang Qing Grand Herald; he entered and left the bedchamber and received and issued edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Lü, Zhang Qing became Grand Herald, passing in and out of the imperial bedchamber to transmit commands.

sentences.zh: 文帝時，有趙谈、北宫伯子，颇见亲幸。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wen there were Zhao Tan and Beigong Bozi, who enjoyed considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: During Wen's reign Zhao Tan and Beigong Bozi were notably favored.

sentences.zh: 至于孝武，亦爱李延年。

translations.literal: As for Emperor Wu, he also favored Li Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu likewise favored Li Yannian.

sentences.zh: 帝数宴后庭，或潜游离馆，故请奏机事，多以宦人主之。

translations.literal: The emperor often feasted in the rear palace or slipped away to roam detached lodges, so petitions on confidential matters were mostly handled by eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor banqueted in the inner quarters or stole away to outlying lodges, so sensitive memorials usually ran through eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 至元帝之世，史游为黄門令，勤心纳忠，有所补益。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan's time, Shi You was Yellow Gate Commandant; he served diligently and offered loyal counsel, to some benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan, Shi You served as Yellow Gate Commandant, working faithfully and offering useful remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 其后弘恭、石显以佞险自进，卒有萧、周之祸，损秽帝德焉。

translations.literal: Later Hong Gong and Shi Xian advanced through flattery and craftiness; in the end came disaster for Xiao Wangzhi and Zhou Kan, tarnishing the emperor's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Gong and Shi Xian rose by sycophancy and intrigue, destroying Xiao Wangzhi and Zhou Kan and staining the throne's moral authority.

sentences.zh: 中兴之初，宦官悉用阉人，不复杂调他士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration, all eunuch posts employed castrates exclusively and no longer mixed in other gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was restored, every eunuch office was restricted to castrated men; outsiders were no longer rotated in.

sentences.zh: 至永平中，始置员数，中常侍四人，小黄門十人。

translations.literal: By the Yongping era quotas were first fixed: four regular palace attendants and ten junior yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongping period first fixed numbers: four regular palace attendants and ten junior yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 和帝即祚幼弱，而窦宪兄弟专总权威，内外臣僚，莫由亲接，所与居者，唯庵宦而已。

translations.literal: The He Emperor was young and weak at his accession, while Dou Xian and his brothers monopolized authority; officials within and without had no access to audience, and those who dwelt with him were only eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He mounted the throne as a child; Dou Xian and his brothers held all power, so ministers could not reach him—only eunuchs shared his daily company.

sentences.zh: 故鄭众得专谋禁中，终除大憝，遂享分土之封，超登宫卿之位。

translations.literal: Therefore Zheng Zhong could plot alone within the forbidden precincts, finally eliminated the great scourge, received enfeoffment with land, and rose to chief court eunuch rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong could scheme inside the palace, destroy the Dou regime, win a noble fief, and ascend to the summit of eunuch office.

sentences.zh: 于是中官始盛焉。

translations.literal: From this time palace officials began to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-court power began its rise in earnest.

sentences.zh: 自明帝以后，迄乎延平，委用渐大，而其员稍增，中常侍至有十人，小黄門二十人，改以金珰右貂，兼领卿署之职。

translations.literal: From Emperor Ming through Yanping, reliance on them gradually grew and their numbers slowly increased: regular palace attendants reached ten, junior yellow gates twenty; they changed to gold pendants and right-side martens and concurrently headed ministerial bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: From Ming to Yanping their role deepened—ten regular attendants, twenty junior yellow gates—now with gold seals and right martens, often doubling as heads of regular ministries.

sentences.zh: 邓后以女主临政，而万机殷远，朝臣國议，无由参断帷幄，称制下令，不出房闱之间，不得不委用刑人，寄之國命。

translations.literal: Empress Deng ruled as female sovereign; myriad affairs pressed while court debate could not be settled from behind the curtain—orders issued in her name never left the women's quarters, so she had no choice but to entrust the "punished persons" with the fate of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Deng governed from the harem; policy never left the inner chambers, so she had to hand real authority to eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 手握王爵，口含天宪，非复掖廷永巷之职，闺牖房闼之任也。

translations.literal: They grasped noble ranks in hand and held the imperial mandate in their mouths—no longer merely gatekeepers of harem corridors or stewards of inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They awarded titles and spoke with the force of statute—far beyond the old duties of rear-palace overseers.

sentences.zh: 其后孙程定立顺之功，曹腾参建桓之策，续以五侯合谋，梁冀受钺，迹因公正，恩固主心，故中外服从，上下屏气。

translations.literal: Later Sun Cheng earned merit for enthroning Shun; Cao Teng took part in raising Huan; then the Five Marquises conspired and Liang Ji received the minister's axe—because their acts seemed just and they secured the ruler's trust, all submitted and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng placed Shun on the throne; Cao Teng backed Huan; the Five Marquises plotted and Liang Ji took power—all cloaked in legitimacy and royal favor, so the realm obeyed.

sentences.zh: 或称伊、霍之勋，无谢于往载；

translations.literal: Some called their achievements comparable to Yi Yin and Huo Guang's, not inferior to past ages;
translations.idiomatic: Some likened them to Yi Yin and Huo Guang without apology;

sentences.zh: 或谓良、平之画，复兴于当今。

translations.literal: some said the stratagems of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping were reborn in the present.
translations.idiomatic: others said the counsel of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping had returned.

sentences.zh: 虽時有忠公，而竟见排斥。

translations.literal: Though loyal and upright men appeared at times, they were ultimately cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy ministers surfaced now and then but were invariably pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 举动回山海，呼吸变霜露。

translations.literal: Their motions moved mountains and seas; their breath could turn frost to dew.
translations.idiomatic: A gesture could shake the realm; a whisper could decide life and death.

sentences.zh: 阿旨曲求，則光宠三族；

translations.literal: Those who flattered aims and bent to seek favor brought glory to three generations;
translations.idiomatic: Flatter the powerful and your kin for three generations thrive;

sentences.zh: 直情忤意，則参夷五宗。

translations.literal: those who spoke straight and offended were extirpated across five branches of kin.
translations.idiomatic: cross them and five branches of family face the blade.

sentences.zh: 汉之纲纪大乱矣。

translations.literal: The moral order of Han was thrown into utter confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Han governance collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 若夫高冠长剑，纡硃怀金者，布满宫闱；

translations.literal: As for those with tall caps and long swords, vermilion cords and gold seals—they filled palace and harem;
translations.idiomatic: Men in court dress and ritual swords, red ribbons and gold seals, crowded every corridor;

sentences.zh: 苴茅分虎，南面臣人者，盖以十数。

translations.literal: those granted straw bundles and tiger tallies to face south as rulers of men numbered in the tens.
translations.idiomatic: those enfeoffed with regalia to rule as princes ran to dozens.

sentences.zh: 府署第馆，棋列于都鄙；

translations.literal: Their mansions and offices stood arrayed like a chessboard through capital and countryside;
translations.idiomatic: Residences and yamen checkerboarded the capital and the provinces;

sentences.zh: 子弟支附，过半于州國。

translations.literal: their sons, younger kin, and hangers-on held more than half the posts in the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: kinsmen and clients saturated regional office.

sentences.zh: 南金、和宝、冰纨、雾縠之积，盈仞珍藏；

translations.literal: Stores of southern gold, He jewels, ice-white silk, and mist gauze filled treasure vaults to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Southern gold, He pearls, ice silk, mist gauze—treasure rooms stacked to the rafters;

sentences.zh: 嫱媛、侍兒、歌单、舞女之玩，充备绮室。

translations.literal: Concubines, maids, singers, and dancing girls for amusement packed splendid chambers.
translations.idiomatic: concubines, maids, singers, and dancers filled silk-lined halls.

sentences.zh: 狗馬饰雕文，土木被缇绣。

translations.literal: Dogs and horses bore carved trappings; rammed-earth halls wore embroidered damask.
translations.idiomatic: Horses wore chased ornament; halls were draped in brocade.

sentences.zh: 皆剥割萌黎，竞恣奢欲。

translations.literal: All of it was stripped from the common people as they raced to indulge outrageous desires.
translations.idiomatic: All of it was squeezed from the people to feed unrestrained luxury.

sentences.zh: 构害明贤，专树党类。

translations.literal: They framed worthy men and packed offices with their own faction.
translations.idiomatic: They ruined good officials and stacked government with allies.

sentences.zh: 其有更相援引，希附权强者，皆腐身熏子，以自衒达。

translations.literal: Those who mutually recommended one another, hoping to cling to the mighty, castrated themselves and placed heirs to advance their careers.
translations.idiomatic: Climbers castrated themselves and registered sons or protégés to win favor.

sentences.zh: 同敝相济，故其徒有繁，败國蠹败之事，不可单書。

translations.literal: Like leaking vessels bailing one another out, their party grew vast; deeds that ruined and worm-eaten the state cannot be recorded on a single scroll.
translations.idiomatic: They abetted one another until their numbers swelled—crimes that rotted the state outnumbered any chronicle.

sentences.zh: 所以海内嗟毒，志士穷栖，寇剧缘间，摇乱区夏。

translations.literal: Hence all within the seas groaned; men of purpose hid in poverty; bandits seized their chances and shook the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: The empire groaned; talent went into hiding; rebels exploited the chaos and convulsed the heartland.

sentences.zh: 虽忠良怀愤，時或奋发，而言出祸从，旋见孥戮。

translations.literal: Though loyal men nursed rage and sometimes acted, as soon as they spoke disaster followed and they were quickly slaughtered with their families.
translations.idiomatic: Patriots burned with anger and occasionally struck—but speech brought ruin and families died together.

sentences.zh: 因复大考钩党，转相诬染。

translations.literal: Thereupon came great inquisitions into faction ties, and accusation spread from hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the great purges for "faction," denunciation spreading like a contagion.

sentences.zh: 凡称善士，莫不离被灾毒。

translations.literal: Every man reckoned good suffered calamity without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone labeled virtuous was dragged into the net.

sentences.zh: 窦武、何进，位崇戚近，乘九服之嚣怨，协群英之势力，而以疑留不断，至于殄败。

translations.literal: Dou Wu and He Jin held lofty rank as close kin, rode the resentful clamor of the nine circuits, and united the strength of the worthy—yet hesitated and could not decide, until they were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu and He Jin stood high as imperial in-laws and commanded elite support, yet wavered until annihilation.

sentences.zh: 斯亦运之极乎！

translations.literal: Was this not the extreme of the age's fate?
translations.idiomatic: Had fate reached its nadir?

sentences.zh: 虽袁绍龚行，芟夷无余，然以暴易乱，亦何云及！

translations.literal: Though Yuan Shao marched in righteous array and extirpated them without remainder, to replace chaos with violence—what comfort was there in that?
translations.idiomatic: Even when Yuan Shao wiped them out, trading turmoil for brutality hardly counted as restoration.

sentences.zh: 自曹腾说梁冀，竟立昏弱。

translations.literal: From Cao Teng's persuasion of Liang Ji to the enthronement of the weak and dim…
translations.idiomatic: From Cao Teng's advice to Liang Ji enthroning a helpless boy…

sentences.zh: 魏武因之，遂迁龟鼎。

translations.literal: King Wei of Wei seized the occasion and carried off the sacred tripods.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao exploited the opening and seized the mandate.

sentences.zh: 所谓“君以此始，必以此终”，信乎其然矣！

translations.literal: As they say, "What you begin with is how you end"—how true it proved!
translations.idiomatic: "By this you rise, by this you fall"—the proverb held all too true.

sentences.zh: 鄭众字季产，南陽犨人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong, courtesy name Jichan, was a native of Chan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong (courtesy Jichan) came from Chan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 为人谨敏有心几。

translations.literal: By nature he was cautious, quick, and keen-minded.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful, alert, and astute.

sentences.zh: 永平中，初给事太子家。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he first served in the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping he entered service in the crown prince's establishment.

sentences.zh: 肃宗即位，拜小黄門，迁中常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhang ascended the throne, he was appointed junior yellow gate and promoted to regular palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhang took the throne, Zheng became junior yellow gate, then regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 和帝初，加位钩盾令。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor He's reign he was additionally named Vault Shield superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor He he added the post of Vault Shield commandant.

sentences.zh: 時窦太后秉政，后兄大将军宪等并窃威权，朝臣上下莫不附之，而众独一心王室，不事豪党，帝亲信焉。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Dou held power; her brother Grand General Dou Xian and others monopolized authority, and none among officials failed to attach to them—yet Zhong alone kept faith with the royal house and did not serve powerful factions, so the emperor trusted him intimately.
translations.idiomatic: While the Dou clan dominated and everyone curried favor, Zheng Zhong alone backed the throne and won the emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 及宪兄弟图作不轨，众遂首谋诛之，以功迁大长秋。

translations.literal: When the Dou brothers plotted rebellion, Zhong took the lead in plotting their execution and for his merit was promoted to grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dou brothers turned traitor, Zheng masterminded their destruction and rose to grand prolonger of autumn.

sentences.zh: 策勋班赏，每辞多受少。

translations.literal: When merits were tallied and rewards distributed, he always declined much and accepted little.
translations.idiomatic: At every promotion he refused the larger share of honors.

sentences.zh: 由是常与议事。

translations.literal: Henceforth he was constantly consulted in deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He thereafter routinely joined state councils.

sentences.zh: 中官用权，自众始焉。

translations.literal: Palace officials wielding power began with Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch ascendancy began with him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，帝念众功美，封为鄛乡侯，食邑千五百户。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yongyuan the emperor, mindful of Zhong's merit, enfeoffed him as marquis of Zhaoxiang with fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 14 (92 CE) he was enfeoffed as marquis of Zhaoxiang with 1,500 households.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，和熹皇后益封三百户。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, Empress Dowager Deng added three hundred households to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 107 Empress Dowager Deng added 300 households to his estate.

sentences.zh: 元初元年卒，养子闳嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yuanchu; his adopted son Hong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanchu 114; adopted son Hong inherited.

sentences.zh: 闳卒，子安嗣。

translations.literal: Hong died; his son An succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hong died; son An succeeded.

sentences.zh: 后國绝。

translations.literal: Later the fief lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate later died out.

sentences.zh: 桓帝延熹二年，绍封众曾孙石雠为关内侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxi of Emperor Huan, Zhong's great-grandson Shi Chou was again enfeoffed as secondary marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 2 of Emperor Huan his great-grandson Shi Chou was again enfeoffed as a secondary marquis.

sentences.zh: 伦有才學，尽心敦慎，数犯严颜，匡弼得失。

translations.literal: Lun had talent and learning; he was wholeheartedly earnest and cautious, often risked the emperor's anger, and corrected policy errors.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Lun was learned and diligent, often spoke against the sovereign's mood, and remedied mistakes.

sentences.zh: 每至休沐，辄闭門绝宾，暴体田野。

translations.literal: Whenever his rest day came, he shut his gates and refused visitors, working shirtless in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: On mandated rest days he barred his gates and labored stripped in the open fields.

sentences.zh: 后加位尚方令。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to director of the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: He later became director of the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 永元九年，监作秘剑及诸器械，莫不精工坚密，为后世法。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongyuan he supervised construction of secret swords and various weapons; none were not exquisitely firm and fine, setting a model for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 97 he oversaw secret blades and ordnance—every piece was superb and became a standard for posterity.

sentences.zh: 元初元年，邓太后以伦久宿卫，封为龍亭侯，邑三百户。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanchu, Empress Dowager Deng, because Lun had long guarded the palace, enfeoffed him as marquis of Longting with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanchu 114 Empress Dowager Deng made him marquis of Longting (300 households) for long palace service.

sentences.zh: 后为长乐太仆。

translations.literal: Later he became grand coachman of Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as grand coachman of Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝以經傳之文多不正定，乃选通儒谒者劉珍及博士良史诣东观，各雠校汉家法，令伦监典其事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanchu the emperor, because texts of the classics were often corrupt, selected the learned herald Liu Zhen and erudite historians to go to the Eastern Pavilion and collate Han jurisprudence in turn, ordering Lun to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanchu 4 (117 CE) the emperor sent Liu Zhen and scholars to the Eastern Pavilion to collate the canon; Lun directed the project.

sentences.zh: 伦初受窦后讽旨，诬陷安帝祖母宋贵人。

translations.literal: At first Lun had followed Empress Dowager Dou's hint and falsely accused Emperor An's grandmother, the Honored Lady Song.
translations.idiomatic: Lun had once framed Emperor An's grandmother Lady Song at Dou's orders.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，安帝始亲万机，敕使自致廷尉。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, Emperor An began personally to handle myriad affairs and ordered Lun to surrender himself to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, An took power and ordered Lun to deliver himself to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 伦耻受辱，乃沐浴整衣冠，饮药而死。

translations.literal: Lun was ashamed to suffer humiliation; he bathed, straightened cap and robes, and drank poison.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, dressed formally, and took poison rather than face trial.

sentences.zh: 國除。

translations.literal: The fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate was revoked.

sentences.zh: 孙程字稚卿，涿郡新城人也。

translations.literal: Sun Cheng, courtesy name Zhiqing, was a native of Xincheng in Zhuojun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng (courtesy Zhiqing) was from Xincheng in Zhuojun.

sentences.zh: 安帝時，为中黄門，给事长乐宫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor An he was central yellow gate and served Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An he served as central yellow gate at Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 時邓太后临朝，帝不亲政事。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng faced the court; the emperor did not personally handle government.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Deng held court; the emperor did not rule in person.

sentences.zh: 小黄門李閏与帝乳母王聖常共谮太后兄执金吾悝等，言欲废帝，立平原王翼，帝每忿惧。

translations.literal: Junior yellow gate Li Run and the emperor's wet nurse Wang Sheng constantly slandered the empress dowager's brother Bearer of the Golden Mallet Deng Kui and others, saying they wished to depose the emperor and establish Prince Yi of Pingyuan; the emperor was often furious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Li Run and wet nurse Wang Sheng slandered Deng Kui, claiming the Dengs meant to depose the emperor for Prince Yi—the emperor lived in rage and dread.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，遂诛邓氏而废平原王，封閏雍乡侯；

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, they executed the Deng clan and deposed the Prince of Pingyuan; Run was enfeoffed as marquis of Yongxiang;
translations.idiomatic: When she died the Dengs were slaughtered and Prince Yi cast aside; Li Run became marquis of Yongxiang;

sentences.zh: 又小黄門江京以谗谄进，初迎帝于邸，以功封都乡侯，食邑各三百户。

translations.literal: moreover junior yellow gate Jiang Jing advanced through slander and flattery; he had first welcomed the emperor at the royal residence, and for merit was enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jing, who had welcomed An from his princely residence, was made marquis of Duxiang with 300 households.

sentences.zh: 閏、京并迁中常侍，江京兼大长秋，与中常侍樊丰、黄門令劉安、钩盾令陳达及王聖、聖女伯荣扇动内外，竞为侈虐。

translations.literal: Run and Jing were both promoted to regular palace attendants; Jiang Jing also served as grand prolonger of autumn, together with regular attendant Fan Feng, yellow gate commandant Liu An, vault shield commandant Chen Da, and Wang Sheng and Sheng's daughter Borong, who stirred court and harem and vied in cruelty and excess.
translations.idiomatic: Li Run and Jiang rose to chief eunuchs; with Fan Feng, Liu An, Chen Da, and Wang Sheng's circle they terrorized inside and out.

sentences.zh: 又帝舅大将军耿宝、皇后兄大鸿胪阎显更相阿党，遂枉殺太尉杨震，废皇太子为济陰王。

translations.literal: Moreover the emperor's uncle Grand General Geng Bao and the empress's elder brother Minister Honglu Yan Xian formed a mutual clique, wrongly executed Grand Commandant Yang Zhen, and demoted the crown prince to prince of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bao and Yan Xian colluded, executed Yang Zhen, and reduced the heir to Prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 明年帝崩，立北乡侯为天子。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died; they installed the Marquis of Beixiang as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The next year An died and the Beixiang marquis was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 显等遂专朝争权，乃讽有司奏诛樊丰，废耿宝、王聖，及党与皆见死徙。

translations.literal: Yan Xian and others then monopolized the court; they induced officials to memorialize killing Fan Feng and demoting Geng Bao and Wang Sheng, and their associates all suffered death or banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xian's faction then purged Fan Feng, Geng Bao, and Wang Sheng, executing or exiling their allies.

sentences.zh: 阎显時在禁中，忧迫不知所为，小黄門樊登劝显发兵，以太后詔召越骑校尉冯詩、虎贲中郎将阎崇，屯朔平門，以御程等。

translations.literal: Yan Xian was inside the forbidden precincts, anxious and at a loss; junior yellow gate Fan Deng urged him to mobilize troops, and with the empress dowager's edict summoned Colonel of Agile Cavalry Feng Shi and General of Household Rapid As Yan Chong to camp at Shuoping Gate to oppose Cheng's party.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped in the palace, Yan Xian panicked; Fan Deng urged him to summon Feng Shi and Yan Chong to Shuoping Gate against Sun Cheng.

sentences.zh: 诱詩入省，太后使授之印，曰：“能得济陰王者封万户侯，得李閏者五千户侯。

translations.literal: They lured Feng Shi into the palace; the empress dowager had him invested with the seal, saying: "Whoever captures the Prince of Jiyin will be marquis of ten thousand households; whoever captures Li Run, five thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: They tricked Feng Shi inside; the offer was 10,000 households for the Prince of Jiyin and 5,000 for Li Run.

sentences.zh: ”显以詩所将众少，使与登迎吏士于左掖門外。

translations.literal: Yan Xian, because the force Feng Shi led was small, sent him with Fan Deng to rally officers outside the left-side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Feng with Fan Deng to gather troops outside the left palace gate—too few men.

sentences.zh: 詩因格殺登，归营屯守。

translations.literal: Feng Shi thereupon struck and killed Fan Deng and returned to camp to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shi killed Fan Deng on the spot and withdrew to his camp.

sentences.zh: 显弟卫尉景遽从省中还外府，收兵至盛德門。

translations.literal: Yan Xian's younger brother Jing, minister of the guards, hurried from the palace to the outer office and gathered troops to Shengde Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jing rushed from the palace, raised troops, and reached Shengde Gate.

sentences.zh: 程傳召诸尚書使收景。

translations.literal: Sun Cheng sent summons to the masters of writing ordering them to seize Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest Yan Jing.

sentences.zh: 尚書郭镇時卧病，聞之，即率直宿羽林出南止車門，逢景从吏士，拔白刃，呼白：“无干兵。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Guo Zhen was ill in bed; hearing this, he immediately led on-duty royal guards out South Stop-Chariot Gate, met Jing with his officers and men, drew his blade, and shouted: "No unauthorized weapons."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhen, though sick, led palace guards out South Stop-Chariot Gate, drew sword, and shouted for the troops to stand down.

sentences.zh: ”镇即下車，持节詔之。

translations.literal: Zhen immediately dismounted, held the imperial baton, and pronounced edict to them.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and read the imperial order.

sentences.zh: 景曰：“何等詔？

translations.literal: Jing said: "What sort of edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jing asked, "What edict is this?"

sentences.zh: ”因聽镇，不中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listened to Zhen but did not strike true.
translations.idiomatic: He obeyed Zhen’s words but failed to connect.

sentences.zh: 镇引剑击景墯車，左右以戟叉其匈，遂禽之，送廷尉狱，即夜死。

translations.literal: Zhen drew his sword and struck Jing, tumbling him from the chariot; attendants on left and right crossed halberds at his breast and seized him, sent him to the commandant of justice’s prison, and that night he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhen struck Yan Jing from his carriage; guards pinned him with halberds, took him to jail, and he died overnight.

sentences.zh: 旦日，令侍御史收显等送狱，于是遂定。

translations.literal: At dawn the emperor ordered the imperial clerk to arrest Yan Xian and the others and send them to prison; thereupon order was settled.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn imperial clerks seized Yan Xian’s faction; with that the coup was secure.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict stating

sentences.zh: 夫表功录善，古今之通义也。

translations.literal: To display merit and record goodness is the universal principle from antiquity to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Recording virtue and rewarding merit is the constant duty of every age.

sentences.zh: 故中常侍长乐太仆江京、黄門令劉安、钩盾令陳达与故車骑将军阎显兄弟谋议恶逆，倾乱天下。

translations.literal: Therefore the late regular attendant and grand coachman of Changle Jiang Jing, yellow gate commandant Liu An, vault shield commandant Chen Da, and the late chariot-and-cavalry general Yan Xian and his brothers plotted wicked rebellion and overturned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The late Jiang Jing, Liu An, Chen Da, and General Yan Xian conspired in treason and threw the empire into chaos.

sentences.zh: 中黄門孙程、王康、长乐太官丞王國、、中黄門黄龍、彭恺、孟叔、李建、王成、張贤、史汎、馬國、王道、李元、杨佗、陳予、趙封、李刚、魏猛、苗光等，怀忠愤发，戮力协谋，遂埽灭元恶，以定王室。

translations.literal: Central yellow gate Sun Cheng, Wang Kang, assistant director of Changle Palace Wang Guo, central yellow gates Huang Long, Peng Kai, Meng Shu, Li Jian, Wang Cheng, Zhang Xian, Shi Fan, Ma Guo, Wang Dao, Li Yuan, Yang Tuo, Chen Yu, Zhao Feng, Li Gang, Wei Meng, Miao Guang, and others harbored loyal rage, joined forces in conspiracy, swept away the chief villain, and thereby stabilized the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng and eighteen fellow eunuchs mustered loyal resolve, acted together, destroyed the ringleaders, and restored the throne.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎：“无言不雠，元德不报。

translations.literal: Does not the Book of Songs say: "No word goes unanswered; no supreme virtue goes unrewarded?"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs asks: "What speech goes unanswered? What highest virtue lacks its reward?"

sentences.zh: ”程为谋首，康、國协同。

translations.literal: Cheng was chief plotter; Kang and Guo coordinated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng led the plot; Wang Kang and Wang Guo assisted.

sentences.zh: 其封程为浮陽侯，食邑五户；

translations.literal: Enfeoff Cheng as marquis of Fuyang with ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng was enfeoffed as marquis of Fuyang with ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 康为华容侯，國为郦侯，各九千户；

translations.literal: Kang as marquis of Huarong, Guo as marquis of Li—nine thousand households each;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kang became marquis of Huarong and Wang Guo marquis of Li, each with nine thousand households;

sentences.zh: 黄龍为湘南侯，五千户；

translations.literal: Huang Long as marquis of Xiangnan, five thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Long was marquis of Xiangnan with five thousand households;

sentences.zh: 彭恺为西平昌侯，孟叔为中庐侯，李建为复陽侯，各四千二百户；

translations.literal: Peng Kai as marquis of Xipingchang, Meng Shu as marquis of Zhonglu, Li Jian as marquis of Fuyang—four thousand two hundred households each;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Kai, Meng Shu, and Li Jian held marquisates of four thousand two hundred households each;

sentences.zh: 王成为广宗侯，張贤为祝阿侯，史汎为临沮侯，馬國为文平侯，王道为范县侯，李元为褒信侯，杨佗为山都侯，陳予为下隽侯，趙封为析县侯，李刚为枝江侯，各四千户；

translations.literal: Wang Cheng as marquis of Guangzong, Zhang Xian as marquis of Zhu’a, Shi Fan as marquis of Linju, Ma Guo as marquis of Wenping, Wang Dao as marquis of Fan County, Li Yuan as marquis of Baoxin, Yang Tuo as marquis of Shandu, Chen Yu as marquis of Xiajuan, Zhao Feng as marquis of Xi County, Li Gang as marquis of Zhijiang—four thousand households each;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, Zhang Xian, Shi Fan, Ma Guo, Wang Dao, Li Yuan, Yang Tuo, Chen Yu, Zhao Feng, and Li Gang each held four thousand households;

sentences.zh: 魏猛为夷陵侯，二千户；

translations.literal: Wei Meng as marquis of Yiling, two thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Meng was marquis of Yiling with two thousand households;

sentences.zh: 苗光为东阿侯，千户。

translations.literal: Miao Guang as marquis of Dong’e, one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Guang was marquis of Dong’e with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 是为十九侯。

translations.literal: These make up the nineteen marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Thus arose the celebrated nineteen marquises.

sentences.zh: 加赐車、馬、金、银、钱、帛，各有差。

translations.literal: There were additional gifts of carriages, horses, gold, silver, cash, and silks in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The court added graded gifts of vehicles, horses, bullion, coin, and silk.

sentences.zh: 李閏以先不豫谋，故不封。

translations.literal: Li Run, because he had not joined the plot beforehand, received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Run was excluded from the rewards because he had not shared in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 遂擢拜程骑都尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cheng was promoted to chief commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng was elevated to chief commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永建元年，程与張贤、孟叔、馬國等为司隶校尉虞诩讼罪，怀表上殿，呵叱左右。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongjian, Cheng together with Zhang Xian, Meng Shu, Ma Guo, and others pleaded for Metropolitan Superintendent Yu Xu and bore memorials into the hall, rebuking attendants left and right.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 126 Sun Cheng and allies petitioned for Yu Xu, marched into the hall with memorials, and shouted down the courtiers.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遂免程官，因悉遣十九侯就國，后徙封程为宜城侯。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, dismissed Cheng from office, sent all nineteen marquises away to their fiefs, and later transferred Cheng’s title to marquis of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Sun Cheng’s post, banished all nineteen nobles to their estates, and later moved Sun Cheng’s enfeoffment to Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 程既到國，怨恨恚怼，封还印绶、符策，亡归京师，往來山中。

translations.literal: Once Cheng reached his fief he nursed resentment and outrage, returned seals and tallies, fled back to the capital, and moved back and forth in the hills.
translations.idiomatic: At his domain Sun Cheng brooded, surrendered his insignia, fled to Luoyang, and hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 詔書追求，复故爵士，赐車馬衣物，遣还國。

translations.literal: Edicts pursued him; his former noble rank was restored, carriages, horses, and clothing were granted, and he was sent back to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial messengers fetched him back, restored his title and gifts, and escorted him home.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝念程等功勋，悉征还京师。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor, mindful of Cheng’s merit, summoned them all back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongjian the court recalled the entire group to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 程与王道、李元皆拜骑都尉，余悉奉朝请。

translations.literal: Cheng together with Wang Dao and Li Yuan were all appointed chief commandants of cavalry; the rest received nominal court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng, Wang Dao, and Li Yuan became chief commandants of cavalry; the others held sinecure appointments.

sentences.zh: 陽嘉元年，程病甚，即拜奉車都尉，位特进。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yangjia Cheng fell gravely ill and was immediately appointed chief commandant of chariots with specially advanced rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Yangjia 132 a dying Sun Cheng received the supernumerary post of chief commandant of chariots.

sentences.zh: 及卒，使五官中郎将追赠車骑将军印绶，赐谥刚侯。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor sent the leader of court gentlemen for all purposes to posthumously award seals of general of chariots and cavalry and bestowed the posthumous title Marquis Gang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the court sent an envoy with seals of general of chariots and cavalry and canonized him as Marquis Gang.

sentences.zh: 侍御史持节监护丧事，乘舆幸北部尉傳，瞻望車骑。

translations.literal: An imperial clerk with baton supervised the funeral; the imperial carriage visited the northern precinct captain’s lodge to gaze upon the chariot-and-cavalry procession.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant clerk oversaw the obsequies while the emperor drove to the northern captain’s station to view the cortège.

sentences.zh: 程临终，遗言上書，以國傳弟美。

translations.literal: At life’s end Cheng left a memorial asking that his domain pass to his younger brother Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng’s dying memorial asked to transmit his fief to his brother Mei.

sentences.zh: 帝许之，而分程半，封程养子寿为浮陽侯。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed but halved Cheng’s territory and enfeoffed Cheng’s adopted son Shou as marquis of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved but split the estate, naming adopted son Sun Shou marquis of Fuyang for half the income.

sentences.zh: 后詔書录微功，封兴渠为高望亭侯。

translations.literal: Later an edict noted minor merit and enfeoffed Xing Qu as marquis of Gaowangting.
translations.idiomatic: A later edict rewarded lesser service and made Xing Qu marquis of Gaowangting.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔宦官养子悉聽得为后，袭封爵，定著乎令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict declared that adopted sons of eunuchs might all serve as heirs, inherit noble ranks, and this was fixed in ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year edicts allowed every eunuch’s adopted heir to succeed and inherit titles—written into law.

sentences.zh: 王康、王國、彭恺、王成、趙封、魏猛六人皆早卒。

translations.literal: Wang Kang, Wang Guo, Peng Kai, Wang Cheng, Zhao Feng, and Wei Meng all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Six of the nineteen—Wang Kang, Wang Guo, Peng Kai, Wang Cheng, Zhao Feng, and Wei Meng—died early.

sentences.zh: 黄龍、杨佗、孟叔、李建、張贤、史汎、王道、李元，李刚九人与阿母山陽君宋娥更相货赂，求高官增邑，又诬罔中常侍曹腾、孟贲等。

translations.literal: Huang Long, Yang Tuo, Meng Shu, Li Jian, Zhang Xian, Shi Fan, Wang Dao, Li Yuan, and Li Gang—nine men—together with the emperor’s foster mother, Lady Song E of Shanyang, exchanged bribes to seek higher offices and larger fiefs, and also falsely accused regular attendant Cao Teng and Meng Ben of misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Nine marquises colluded with Lady Song E to buy promotions and slander Cao Teng and Meng Ben.

sentences.zh: 永和二年，发觉，并遣就國，减祖四分之一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghe the plot surfaced; all were ordered to their fiefs and lost one quarter of rent income.
translations.idiomatic: When exposed in Yonghe 137 they were sent home and forfeited a quarter of their revenues.

sentences.zh: 宋娥夺爵归田舍。

translations.literal: Lady Song was stripped of rank and returned to her farmhouse.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song lost her title and went back to farm life.

sentences.zh: 唯馬國、陳予、苗光保全封邑。

translations.literal: Only Ma Guo, Chen Yu, and Miao Guang kept their full enfeoffments intact.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guo, Chen Yu, and Miao Guang alone retained intact estates.

sentences.zh: 初，帝见废，监太子家小黄門籍建、傅高梵、长秋长趙熹、丞良贺、药长夏珍皆以无过获罪，建等坐徙朔方。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor had been deposed, junior yellow gate Ji Jian who supervised the heir’s household, Fu Gaofan, Chief of the Long Autumn Zhao Xi, Assistant Director Liang He, and Pharmacy Director Xia Zhen had all been punished though guiltless; Ji and the others were banished to Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was earlier removed, Ji Jian, Fu Gaofan, Zhao Xi, Liang He, and Xia Zhen suffered though innocent and were exiled to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，并擢为中常侍。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne they were all promoted to regular palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At his restoration they became chief eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 梵坐臧罪，减死一等。

translations.literal: Fan sat convicted of embezzlement and had his sentence reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gaofan took a corruption conviction commuted one grade.

sentences.zh: 建后封东乡侯，三百户。

translations.literal: Ji was later enfeoffed as marquis of Dongxiang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jian later became marquis of Dongxiang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 贺清俭退厚，位至大长秋。

translations.literal: He was pure, frugal, modest, and thick-skinned in withdrawal, rising to grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Liang He lived plainly and rose to grand prolonger of autumn.

sentences.zh: 陽嘉中，詔九卿举武猛，贺独无所荐。

translations.literal: During Yangjia an edict ordered the nine ministers to recommend fierce warriors; He alone recommended no one.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers had to nominate fierce fighters, Liang He nominated nobody.

sentences.zh: 帝引问其故，对曰：“臣生自草茅，长于宫掖，既无知人之明，又未尝交知士类。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him and asked why; he replied: "Your servant was born among weeds and grew up in palace corridors; I lack insight to judge men and have never mingled with gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for his reasons he said, "I grew up an outsider and inside the harem—I neither know talent nor move among scholars."

sentences.zh: 昔卫鞅因景监以见，有识知其不终。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Yang gained audience through Jing Jian; those with discernment knew he would not last.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yang once entered court through Jing Jian; observers knew his rise would not endure.

sentences.zh: 今得臣举者，匪荣伊辱。

translations.literal: Those recommended through me today would win not glory but shame."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone I nominated would earn shame, not honor."

sentences.zh: ”固辞之。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝思贺忠，封其养子为都乡侯，三百户。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor remembered He’s loyalty and enfeoffed his adopted son as marquis of Duxiang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang He died the emperor remembered his loyalty and made his adopted son marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 腾用事省闼三十余年，奉事四帝，未尝有过。

translations.literal: Teng wielded influence within the palace precincts for more than thirty years and served four emperors without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng influenced inner-palace affairs for thirty years and served four sovereigns without blemish.

sentences.zh: 其所进达，皆海内名人，陳留虞放、边韶、南陽延固、張温、弘农張奂、颍川堂谿典等。

translations.literal: Those he recommended and advanced were illustrious men of the realm: Yu Fang of Chenliu, Bian Shao, Yan Gu of Nanyang, Zhang Wen, Zhang Huan of Hongnong, Tangxi Dian of Yingchuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His protégés included Yu Fang, Bian Shao, Yan Gu, Zhang Wen, Zhang Huan, Tangxi Dian—celebrities empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 時蜀郡太守因计吏赂遗于腾，益州刺史种暠于斜谷关搜得其書，上奏太守，并以劾腾，请下廷尉案罪。

translations.literal: At that time the governor of Shu Commandery sent bribes to Teng through the clerk presenting accounts; Inspector Chong Gao of Yi Province seized the letter at Xiegu Pass and memorialized against both governor and Teng, asking the commandant of justice to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When a Shu governor tried to bribe Cao Teng via the accounting clerk, Inspector Chong Gao intercepted the letter at Xiegu Pass and impeached both men.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“書自外來，非腾之过。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The letter came from outside; it is not Teng’s fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The missive came from beyond the palace—Cao Teng is blameless."

sentences.zh: ”遂寝暠奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhong’s memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Gao’s accusation was dropped.

sentences.zh: 腾不为纤介，常称暠为能吏，時人嗟美之。

translations.literal: Teng bore no grudge over trifles and always praised Zhong as a capable official; people of the time sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng nursed no petty spite and publicly praised Chong Gao as an able officer—winning widespread admiration.

sentences.zh: 腾卒，养子嵩嗣。

translations.literal: When Teng died his adopted son Song succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng died; adopted son Cao Song inherited.

sentences.zh: 种暠后为司徒，告宾客曰：“今身为公，乃曹常侍力焉。

translations.literal: Later Chong became minister of education and told guests: "Today I stand as one of the Three Dukes thanks to Attendant Cao."
translations.idiomatic: Years later Chong Gao became steward and told guests, "My elevation owes everything to Attendant Cao."

translations.literal: [Closing the quotation begun above.]
translations.idiomatic: (End of Chong Gao’s remark.)

sentences.zh: 嵩靈帝時货赂中官及输西园钱一亿万，故位至太尉。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ling Cao Song bribed inner officials and paid over one hundred million cash into the Western Garden treasury, hence rose to grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Lingdi Cao Song bought eunuchs and poured a hundred million cash into the Western Garden fund to reach grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 及子操起兵，不肯相随，乃与少子疾避乱琅邪，为徐州刺史陶谦所殺。

translations.literal: When his son Cao Cao raised troops Song refused to follow him and fled with a younger son to Langye for refuge; the provincial governor Tao Qian killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When warlords rose Cao Song refused to join Cao Cao, fled toward Langye with a younger son, and Tao Qian’s men cut him down.

sentences.zh: 单超、徐璜、具瑗、左悺、唐衡

translations.literal: Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Guan, Tang Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Guan, and Tang Heng—the five men later known as the Five Marquises.

sentences.zh: 单超，河南人；

translations.literal: Shan Chao was a man of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Chao came from Henan;

sentences.zh: 徐璜，下邳良城人；

translations.literal: Xu Huang was a man of Liangcheng in Xiapi;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang hailed from Liangcheng in Xiapi;

sentences.zh: 具瑗，魏郡元城人；

translations.literal: Ju Yuan was a man of Yuancheng in Wei Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yuan came from Yuancheng in Wei Commandery;

sentences.zh: 左悺，河南平陰人；

translations.literal: Zuo Guan was a man of Pingyin in Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guan was from Pingyin in Henan;

sentences.zh: 唐衡，颍川郾人也。

translations.literal: Tang Heng was a man of Yan in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Heng came from Yan in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 桓帝初，超、璜、瑗为中常侍，悺、衡为小黄門史。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Huan’s reign Chao, Huang, and Yuan were regular palace attendants while Guan and Tang served as junior yellow gate clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Early under Huan, Shan Chao, Xu Huang, and Ju Yuan were chief attendants; Zuo Guan and Tang Heng were junior yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 初，梁冀两妹为顺、桓二帝皇后，冀代父商为大将军，再世权威，威振天下。

translations.literal: Originally Liang Ji’s two younger sisters were empresses to Emperors Shun and Huan; Ji succeeded his father Shang as grand general and for two generations wielded authority that shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji’s two sisters wed Shun and Huan; he inherited his father’s generalship and dominated two reigns.

sentences.zh: 冀自诛太尉李固、杜乔等，骄横益甚，皇后乘势忌恣，多所鸩毒，上下钳口，莫有言者。

translations.literal: After Ji executed Grand Commandant Li Gu and Du Qiao his arrogance grew worse; the empress exploited her position to indulge jealousy and poison freely; high and low sealed their lips—none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering Li Gu and Du Qiao Liang Ji grew wilder; his queen sister poisoned rivals while everyone stayed mute.

sentences.zh: 帝逼畏久，恒怀不平，恐言泄，不敢谋之。

translations.literal: The emperor long lived in fear and nursed grievance yet dreaded leaks and dared not plot.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan trembled for years, nursing hatred yet afraid to breathe a word.

sentences.zh: 延熹二年，皇后崩，帝因如厕，独呼衡问：“左右与外舍不相得者皆谁乎？

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxi the empress died; the emperor took occasion while visiting the privy to call Tang Heng alone and asked: "Who among those around me and the consort kin are not getting along?"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died in Yanxi 159 Huan cornered Tang Heng in the lavatory and asked who opposed the Liang clan.

sentences.zh: ”衡对曰：“单超、左悺前诣河南尹不疑，礼敬小简，不疑收其兄弟送洛陽狱，二人诣門谢，乃得解。

translations.literal: Heng replied: "Shan Chao and Zuo Guan once visited Prefect of Henan Yin Liang Buyi with slight ceremony; Buyi arrested their brothers and sent them to Luoyang prison; the two came to the gate to apologize before they were freed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Heng said Shan Chao and Zuo Guan once insulted Prefect Liang Buyi, who jailed their brothers until they groveled at his gate.

sentences.zh: 徐璜、具瑗常私忿疾外舍放横，口不敢道。

translations.literal: Xu Huang and Ju Yuan constantly bore private hatred toward the consort kin’s arrogance yet dared not speak aloud."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang and Ju Yuan secretly loathed the Liangs but stayed silent."

sentences.zh: ”于是帝呼超、悺入室，谓曰：“梁将军兄弟专固國朝，迫胁外内，公卿以下从其风旨。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor summoned Chao and Guan indoors and said: "General Liang and his brothers monopolize the court, coercing inside and outside; ministers down to the clerks follow their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Huan then brought Shan Chao and Zuo Guan inside: "The Liangs own the court—everyone obeys them."

sentences.zh: 今欲诛之，于常侍意何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to execute them—what do you attendants think?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to kill them—will you help?"

sentences.zh: ”超等对曰：“诚國奸贼，当诛日久。

translations.literal: Chao and the others replied: "They are indeed traitors to the state and ought long ago to have been executed.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "They are traitors long overdue for execution."

sentences.zh: 臣等弱劣，未知聖意何如耳。

translations.literal: Your servants are weak and mean and do not yet know Your Majesty’s intent."
translations.idiomatic: We are powerless until we know your resolve."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“审然者，常侍密图之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If it is truly so, attendants should secretly plot it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then plot it in secret."

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“图之不难，但恐陛下复中狐疑。

translations.literal: They replied: "Plotting is not hard—we fear only that Your Majesty will again harbor doubts midway."
translations.idiomatic: They feared he might waver midway.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“奸臣胁國，当伏其罪，何疑乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A traitorous minister coercing the state ought to suffer his crime—what doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan snapped, "A traitor squeezing the throne deserves death—no doubts!"

sentences.zh: ”于是更召璜、瑗等五人，遂定其议，帝啮超臂出血为盟，于是超收冀及宗亲党与悉诛之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he further summoned Huang, Yuan, and the other five men; they settled the plan; the emperor bit Chao’s arm until it bled to seal the oath; thereupon Chao arrested Ji and executed him together with kinsmen and clients.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned the full quintet, swore an oath in blood, and Shan Chao seized Liang Ji and extirpated his clan.

sentences.zh: 悺、衡迁中常侍。

translations.literal: Guan and Tang were promoted to regular palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guan and Tang Heng became chief attendants.

sentences.zh: 封超新丰侯，二万户，璜武原侯，瑗东武陽侯，各万五千户，赐钱各千五百万；

translations.literal: Chao was enfeoffed marquis of Xinfeng with twenty thousand households; Huang marquis of Wuyuan and Yuan marquis of Dongwuyang—fifteen thousand households each—with fifteen million cash gifts each;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Chao took Xinfeng with twenty thousand households; Xu Huang and Ju Yuan took fifteen thousand each plus fifteen million cash;

sentences.zh: 悺上蔡侯，衡汝陽侯，各万三千户，赐钱各千三百万。

translations.literal: Guan marquis of Shangcai and Tang marquis of Ruyang—thirteen thousand households each—with thirteen million cash gifts each.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guan and Tang Heng held thirteen thousand households and thirteen million cash apiece.

sentences.zh: 五人同日封，故世谓之“五侯”。

translations.literal: All five were enfeoffed the same day; hence the world calls them the "Five Marquises."
translations.idiomatic: Their simultaneous investiture coined the nickname "Five Marquises."

sentences.zh: 又封小黄門劉普、趙忠等八人为乡侯。

translations.literal: Moreover junior yellow gates Liu Pu, Zhao Zhong, and eight others were enfeoffed as village marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Eight lesser eunuchs including Liu Pu and Zhao Zhong won village marquisates.

sentences.zh: 自是权归宦官，朝廷日乱矣。

translations.literal: From this power rested with eunuchs and the court grew daily more chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth eunuchs held the reins and Han slid deeper into disorder.

sentences.zh: 超病，帝遣使者就拜車骑将军。

translations.literal: When Chao fell ill the emperor dispatched envoys to appoint him general of chariots and cavalry at his bedside.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan Chao sickened the emperor invested him as general of chariots and cavalry in person.

sentences.zh: 明年薨，赐东园秘器，棺中玉具，赠侯将军印绶，使者理丧。

translations.literal: The next year he died; he was granted Eastern Garden secret burial gear, jade fittings inside the coffin, posthumous seals of a general, and envoys managed the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year with imperial grave goods, jade shroud fittings, and general’s insignia.

sentences.zh: 及葬，发五营骑士，侍御史护丧，将作大匠起冢茔。

translations.literal: At burial five camp horsemen were mobilized, imperial clerks guarded the cortège, and the minister of works raised mound and vault.
translations.idiomatic: Burial drew palace cavalry, supervising clerks, and the minister of works to build the tomb.

sentences.zh: 其后四侯转横，天下为之評曰：“左回天，具独坐，徐卧虎，唐两墯。

translations.literal: Thereafter the four marquises grew ever more overbearing; the realm fashioned a rhyme about them: "Zuo turns heaven round; Ju sits alone; Xu is the crouching tiger; Tang has two falls."
translations.idiomatic: People sang of the survivors: "Zuo spins the sky, Ju sits alone, Xu crouches like a tiger, Tang strikes twice."

sentences.zh: ”皆竞起第宅，楼观壮丽，穷极伎巧。

translations.literal: All vied to raise mansions with towering belvederes, magnificent beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: They raced to build mansions and towers of breathtaking luxury.

sentences.zh: 金银罽<耳毛>，施于犬馬。

translations.literal: Gold and silver, wool rugs and feather ornaments—they draped them on dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They decked dogs and horses with gold, silver, woven rugs, and feathered tack.

sentences.zh: 多取良人美女以为姬妾，皆珍饰华侈，拟則宫人，其仆从皆乘牛車而从列骑。

translations.literal: They seized many commoners’ daughters as concubines, bedecked them like palace women, and their retainers rode ox carts escorted by columns of horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed gentlewomen into harems, dressed them like concubines of the throne, and sent lackeys forth in ox carts with mounted escorts.

sentences.zh: 又养其疏属，或乞嗣异姓，或买苍头为子，并以傳國袭封。

translations.literal: They also raised distant relatives, begged heirs from unrelated surnames, bought slaves as sons, and passed down states and noble titles through them.
translations.idiomatic: They adopted stray kin, purchased heirs, and transmitted noble titles through purchased sons.

sentences.zh: 兄弟姻戚皆宰州临郡，辜较百姓，与盗贼无异。

translations.literal: Brothers and marriage allies held prefectures and faced counties, extorting the people no differently than bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers and in-laws governed provinces like brigands.

sentences.zh: 超弟安为河东太守，弟子匡为济陰太守，璜弟盛为河内太守，悺弟敏为陳留太守，瑗兄恭为沛相，皆为所在蠹害。

translations.literal: Chao’s younger brother An was governor of Hedong; his nephew Kuang was governor of Jiyin; Huang’s younger brother Sheng was governor of Henei; Guan’s younger brother Min was governor of Chenliu; Yuan’s elder brother Gong was chancellor of Pei—all plagued their jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Shan An ruled Hedong, Kuang Jiyin, Huang Sheng Henei, Zuo Min Chenliu, Ju Gong ran Pei—each ravaged his commandery.

sentences.zh: 璜兄子宣为下邳令，暴虐尤甚。

translations.literal: Huang’s nephew Xuan was magistrate of Xiapi and cruelty surpassed all.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang’s nephew Xu Xuan governed Xiapi with singular brutality.

sentences.zh: 先是，求故汝南太守下邳李暠女不能得，及到县，遂将吏卒至暠家，载其女归，戏射殺之，埋著寺内。

translations.literal: Earlier he had sought in vain the daughter of former Runan prefect Li Gao of Xiapi; once he reached the county he led clerks and soldiers to Li’s house, carried off the girl, sportingly shot her dead, and buried her inside the temple precinct.
translations.idiomatic: After failing to win Li Gao’s daughter he seized her as magistrate, shot her for sport, and buried her in the county shrine.

sentences.zh: 時，下邳县属东海，汝南黄浮为东海相，有告言宣者，浮乃收宣家属，无少长悉考之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiapi County belonged to Donghai; Huang Fu of Runan was chancellor of Donghai, and when someone reported Xu Xuan, Fu arrested Xuan’s entire household and interrogated every member regardless of age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiapi lay in Donghai commandery; Chancellor Huang Fu, alerted to Xu Xuan’s crimes, seized his whole clan for questioning.

sentences.zh: 掾史以下固谏争。

translations.literal: Clerks and aides below him firmly remonstrated and disputed the move.
translations.idiomatic: His staff pleaded with him to relent.

sentences.zh: 浮曰：“徐宣國贼，今日殺之，明日坐死，足以瞑目矣。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Xu Xuan is a traitor to the state; if I kill him today and face execution tomorrow, I may still close my eyes in peace."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fu replied, "Xuan is a public enemy—if I execute him today and die tomorrow, I will rest content."

sentences.zh: ”即案宣罪弃市，暴其尸以示百姓，郡中震栗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he tried Xuan’s crime and executed him in the marketplace, exposing the corpse to instruct the common people; the commandery trembled.
translations.idiomatic: He condemned Xuan to public execution and left the corpse exposed—the region shook.

sentences.zh: 璜于是诉怨于帝，帝大怒，浮坐髡钳，输作右校。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huang complained to the emperor; the emperor grew furious, and Fu was sentenced to shaving and iron collar and sent to labor at the Right Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang ran to the throne; Emperor Huan raged and condemned Huang Fu to shaved head, cangue, and hard labor at the Right Engineers.

sentences.zh: 五侯宗族宾客虐遍天下，民不堪命，起为寇贼。

translations.literal: The kindred, retainers, and guests of the Five Marquises tyrannized the realm; the people could not endure and rose as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Their kin and clients terrorized every circuit until peasants turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 七年，衡卒，亦赠車骑将军，如超故事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Tang Heng died and likewise received posthumous appointment as general of chariots and cavalry, following Chao’s precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Tang Heng died and received the same posthumous generalship as Shan Chao.

sentences.zh: 璜卒，赙赠钱布，赐冢茔地。

translations.literal: When Huang died, condolence payments of cash and cloth were granted and burial mound land was given.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang’s funeral brought cash, silk, and a cemetery plot from the court.

sentences.zh: 明年，司隶校尉韩演因奏悺罪恶，及其兄太仆南乡侯称请托州郡，聚敛为奸，宾客放纵，侵犯吏民。

translations.literal: The next year Metropolitan Superintendent Han Yan memorialized Zuo Guan’s crimes and those of his elder brother Minister of Works village marquis Cheng for soliciting commanderies and prefectures, amassing wealth through villainy, and letting retainers run riot against officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yan impeached Zuo Guan and his brother Cheng for pressuring local offices and looting the people.

sentences.zh: 悺、称皆自殺。

translations.literal: Guan and Cheng both committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 演又奏瑗兄沛相恭臧罪，征诣廷尉。

translations.literal: Yan further memorialized Ju Yuan’s elder brother Chancellor of Pei Gong for embezzlement and summoned him to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yan also charged Ju Gong and summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑗诣狱谢，上还东武侯印绶，詔贬为都乡侯，卒于家。

translations.literal: Yuan went to prison to apologize, returned seals of marquis of Dongwuyang, was by edict demoted to marquis of Duxiang, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yuan surrendered his titles, took demotion to village marquis, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 超及璜、衡袭封者，并降为乡侯，租入岁皆三百万，子弟分封者，悉夺爵土。

translations.literal: The heirs who inherited from Chao as well as Huang and Heng were together reduced to village marquises with yearly rent income each of three million cash; younger kin who had received separate enfeoffments all lost noble rank and land.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Chao’s, Xu Huang’s, and Tang Heng’s successors were cut to village marquises on three million cash a year; cadet branches lost everything.

sentences.zh: 劉普等贬为关内侯。

translations.literal: Liu Pu and others were demoted to secondary marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pu’s clique fell to rank-five nobility.

sentences.zh: 侯览者，山陽防东人。

translations.literal: Hou Lan was a man of Fangdong in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan came from Fangdong in Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 桓帝初为中常侍，以佞猾进，倚势贪放，受纳货遗以巨万计。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Huan’s reign he was regular palace attendant; he advanced through flattery and craft, leaned on power to be greedy and unrestrained, and received bribes reckoned in tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He rose as chief attendant by sycophancy, extorted vast bribes, and abused his influence.

sentences.zh: 延熹中，连岁征伐，府帑空虚，乃假百官奉禄，王侯租锐。

translations.literal: During the Yanxi years campaigns ran year after year, treasuries emptied, and official salaries and noble rents were borrowed against.
translations.idiomatic: Endless warfare emptied the treasury; the court borrowed against stipends and noble revenues.

sentences.zh: 览亦上缣五千匹，赐爵关内侯。

translations.literal: Lan also submitted five thousand bolts of silk and was granted rank of secondary marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan donated five thousand bolts of silk and bought a secondary marquisate.

sentences.zh: 又托以与议诛梁冀功，进封高乡侯。

translations.literal: Moreover claiming merit in deliberating Liang Ji’s execution, he was advanced to marquis of Gaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed credit for the Liang Ji coup and advanced to marquis of Gaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 小黄門段珪家在济陰，与览并立田业，近济北界，仆从宾客侵犯百姓，劫掠行旅。

translations.literal: Junior yellow gate Duan Gui’s family was in Jiyin; he and Lan maintained adjoining estates near the Jibei border, and retainers and guests raided commoners and plundered travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Gui’s clan in Jiyin shared estates with Hou Lan; their men robbed locals and travelers along the border.

sentences.zh: 济北相滕延一切收捕，殺数十人，陳尸路衢。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Jibei Teng Yan arrested them wholesale, executed several dozen, and displayed corpses at the crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Jibei Chancellor Teng Yan rounded them up, executed dozens, and left bodies in the streets.

sentences.zh: 览、珪大怨，以事诉帝，延坐多殺无辜，征诣廷尉，免。

translations.literal: Lan and Gui nursed great resentment and complained to the emperor; Yan was judged to have killed many innocents, summoned to the commandant of justice, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan and Duan Gui complained; Teng Yan was accused of excess killing, tried, and ousted.

sentences.zh: 延字伯行，北海人，后为京兆尹，有理名，世称为长者。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Boxing, was a man of Beihai; later he became governor of the capital region and won a reputation for good governance; his generation called him a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yan (courtesy Boxing) from Beihai later governed the capital well and was honored as a worthy elder.

sentences.zh: 览等得此愈放纵。

translations.literal: Lan and the others grew still more unrestrained after this.
translations.idiomatic: Freed of Teng Yan, Hou Lan’s faction ran wilder than ever.

sentences.zh: 览兄参为益州刺史，民有丰富者，辄诬以大逆，皆诛灭之，没入财物，前后累亿计。

translations.literal: Lan’s elder brother Can was inspector of Yi Province; whenever commoners were wealthy he falsely accused them of great treason, executed and extinguished them all, and confiscated property—cumulatively worth hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Hou Can as Yi inspector framed rich families for treason, exterminated them, and seized billions in goods.

sentences.zh: 太尉杨秉奏参，槛車征，于道自殺。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yang Bing memorialized against Can; he was summoned in a cage cart and killed himself en route.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bing impeached Hou Can, who committed suicide on the road to Luoyang in a prisoner wagon.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹袁逢于旅舍，阅参車三百余两，皆金银锦帛珍玩，不可胜数。

translations.literal: Governor of the capital Yuan Feng, at a relay inn, inspected more than three hundred of Can’s carts loaded with gold, silver, brocade, silk, and curiosities beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Feng searched Hou Can’s baggage train—over three hundred carts of treasure.

sentences.zh: 览坐免，旋复复官。

translations.literal: Lan was therefore dismissed but soon restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan lost his post briefly, then regained it.

sentences.zh: 建宁二年，丧母还家，大起茔冢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianning he returned home for his mother’s funeral and raised a vast tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianning 169 he buried his mother with a monumental mound.

sentences.zh: 督邮張俭因举奏览贪侈奢纵，前后请夺人宅三百八十一所，田百一十八顷。

translations.literal: Postal inspector Zhang Jian therefore memorialized Lan’s greed, extravagance, and license—through repeated petitions he had seized 381 residences and 118 qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhang Jian listed Hou Lan’s seizures: 381 houses and 118 qing of land.

sentences.zh: 起立第宅十有六区，皆有高楼池苑，堂阁相望，饰以绮画丹漆之属，制度重深，僭类宫省。

translations.literal: He established sixteen mansion compounds, each with lofty towers and pond gardens; halls and belvederes faced one another, ornamented with painted silk, cinnabar, and lacquer; the scale was deep and layered, rivaling the palace and ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He built sixteen villa complexes with towers, pools, and painted halls that mimicked the imperial style.

sentences.zh: 又豫作寿冢，石椁双阙，高庑百尺，破人居室，发掘坟墓。

translations.literal: Moreover he prepared his tomb in advance with stone outer coffin and paired que towers, hundred-foot galleries—demolishing homes and excavating others’ graves.
translations.idiomatic: He prebuilt a mausoleum with stone sarcophagus and twin watch-towers, tearing down houses and robbing tombs.

sentences.zh: 虏夺良人，妻略妇子，及诸罪衅，请诛之。

translations.literal: He seized commoners’ wives and children and carried off women and boys; together with his other crimes he asked that Lan be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He abducted women and children; Zhang Jian demanded the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 而览伺候遮截，章竟不上。

translations.literal: Yet Lan intercepted couriers and blocked the memorial so it never reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan intercepted the memorial so it never arrived.

sentences.zh: 俭遂破览冢宅，藉没资财，具言罪状。

translations.literal: Jian therefore smashed Lan’s tomb and residences, confiscated his assets, and set forth the full bill of crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian raided the properties and filed the inventory of guilt.

sentences.zh: 又奏览母生時交通宾客，干乱郡國。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that while Lan’s mother had lived she trafficked with retainers and disturbed commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Lady Hou had trafficked with clients and disturbed regional government.

sentences.zh: 复不得御。

translations.literal: Again it did not obtain imperial consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Again the throne refused to act.

sentences.zh: 览遂诬俭为钩党，及故长乐少府李膺、太仆杜密等，皆夷灭之。

translations.literal: Lan thereupon framed Jian as a faction conspirator together with former junior coachman of Changle Li Ying, Minister of Works Du Mi, and others; all were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan denounced Zhang Jian and the "faction" purge swallowed Li Ying, Du Mi, and hundreds more.

sentences.zh: 遂代曹节领长乐太仆。

translations.literal: Thereupon he succeeded Cao Jie as grand coachman of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He then replaced Cao Jie as grand coachman of Changle.

sentences.zh: 熹平元年，有司举奏览专权骄奢，策收印绶，自殺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping (172) officials memorialized that Lan monopolized power and arrogance; he was ordered to surrender seals and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping 172 indictments of Hou Lan’s arrogance forced him to surrender his seals and kill himself.

sentences.zh: 阿党者皆免。

translations.literal: Those who had abetted his faction were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His allies were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 時，窦太后临朝， 后父大将军武与太傅陳蕃谋诛中官， 节与长乐五官史硃瑀、从官史共普、張亮、中黄門王尊、长乐谒者腾是等十七人，共矫詔以长乐食监王甫为黄門令，将兵诛武、蕃等，事已具《蕃》、《武傳》。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Dou faced the court; her father Grand General Dou Wu and Grand Tutor Chen Fan plotted to execute the eunuchs—Jie together with Changle clerk Zhu Yu, attendant clerk Gong Pu, Zhang Liang, central yellow gate Wang Zun, Changle herald Teng Shi, and seventeen others jointly forged an edict appointing Changle provision intendant Wang Fu as yellow gate commandant and led troops to kill Wu and Fan—the affair is fully told in the biographies of Fan and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Wu and Chen Fan moved against the eunuchs, Cao Jie and seventeen accomplices forged an edict (see the Fan and Wu chapters).

sentences.zh: 节迁长乐卫尉，封育陽侯，增邑三千户；

translations.literal: Jie was promoted to captain of Changle guards and enfeoffed as marquis of Yuyang with an additional three thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie became captain of Changle guards and marquis of Yuyang plus three thousand households;

sentences.zh: 甫迁中常侍，黄門令如故；

translations.literal: Fu was promoted to regular palace attendant while retaining yellow gate commandant;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu rose to chief attendant while keeping the yellow gate post;

sentences.zh: 瑀封都乡侯，千五百户；

translations.literal: Yu was enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang with fifteen hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu became marquis of Duxiang with fifteen hundred households;

sentences.zh: 普、亮等五人各三百户；

translations.literal: Pu, Liang, and five others received three hundred households each;
translations.idiomatic: Gong Pu, Zhang Liang, and five others took three hundred households each;

sentences.zh: 余十一人皆为关内侯，岁食租二千斛。

translations.literal: the remaining eleven men all became secondary marquises with yearly grain rents of two thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: eleven lesser men became secondary marquises drawing two thousand hu annually.

sentences.zh: 先是，瑀等陰于明堂中祷皇天曰：“窦氏无道，请皇天辅皇帝诛之，令事必成，天下得宁。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu and others had secretly prayed in the Bright Hall to August Heaven: "The Dou clan is lawless; we beg August Heaven to aid the emperor in executing them—may the deed succeed and the realm find peace."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Yu had prayed at the Bright Hall for Heaven to bless the coup against the Dous.

sentences.zh: ”既诛武等，詔令太官给塞具，赐瑀钱五千万，余各有差，后更封华容侯。

translations.literal: After Wu and the others were executed, an edict ordered the Imperial Kitchen to supply funeral gear and granted Yu fifty million cash—the others in graded amounts—and later he was further enfeoffed as marquis of Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: After the slaughter the court showered Zhu Yu with cash and raised him to marquis of Huarong.

sentences.zh: 二年，节病困，詔拜为車骑将军。

translations.literal: In the second year Jie fell gravely ill and was by edict appointed general of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Year two saw Cao Jie dying; the emperor named him general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 有顷疾瘳，上印绶，罢，复为中常侍，位特进，秩中二千石，寻转大长秋。

translations.literal: Shortly his illness cleared; he returned seals, resigned the generalship, again became regular attendant with specially advanced rank at two thousand shi salary grade, and soon transferred to grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered, resigned the generalship, resumed chief attendant at full two thousand shi, then became grand prolonger of autumn.

sentences.zh: 节遂与王甫等诬奏桓帝弟勃海王悝谋反，诛之。

translations.literal: Jie then together with Wang Fu and others falsely memorialized that Emperor Huan’s younger brother Prince Kai of Bohai plotted rebellion, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and Wang Fu framed Prince Kai of Bohai for treason and killed him.

sentences.zh: 以功封者十二人。

translations.literal: Twelve men received enfeoffment for that merit.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve eunuchs won titles for that “merit.”

sentences.zh: 甫封冠军侯。

translations.literal: Fu was enfeoffed as marquis of Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu became marquis of Champion.

sentences.zh: 节亦增邑四千六百户，并前七千六百户。

translations.literal: Jie also received an additional four thousand six hundred households, totaling seven thousand six hundred together with earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie’s fief grew by forty-six hundred households to seventy-six hundred total.

sentences.zh: 父兄子弟皆为公卿列校、牧守令长，布满天下。

translations.literal: Fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews filled posts as ministers, colonels, shepherds, prefects, and magistrates across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His kin packed every level of government.

sentences.zh: 节弟破石为越骑校尉，越骑营五百妻有美色，破石从求之，五百不敢违，妻执意不肯行，遂自殺。

translations.literal: Jie’s younger brother Poshi was colonel of agile cavalry; a soldier’s wife in the agile camp was beautiful, and Poshi demanded her—the soldier dared not refuse, yet the wife steadfastly refused to go and thereupon killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Poshi coveted a trooper’s wife; she chose suicide over submission.

sentences.zh: 其淫暴无道，多此类也。

translations.literal: His lewd cruelty and lack of principle were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His debauchery matched this pattern countless times.

sentences.zh: 光和二年，司隶校尉陽球奏诛王甫及子长乐少府萌、沛相吉，皆死狱中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guanghe (179) Metropolitan Superintendent Yang Qiu memorialized the execution of Wang Fu together with his son junior coachman of Changle Meng and Chancellor of Pei Ji—all died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu destroyed Wang Fu, his son Wang Meng, and Ji of Pei in prison.

sentences.zh: 時连有灾异，郎中梁人审忠以为硃瑀等罪恶所感，乃上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time calamities followed one another in succession; Palace Gentleman Shen Zhong of Liang believed they were stirred by Zhu Yu’s crimes and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ill omens multiplied; Shen Zhong of Liang blamed Zhu Yu’s crimes and submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 章寝不报。

translations.literal: The memorial was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: It vanished into silence.

sentences.zh: 节遂领尚書令。

translations.literal: Jie thereupon headed the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie became Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，赠車骑将军。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died and was posthumously awarded general of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year four with posthumous generalship.

sentences.zh: 后瑀亦病卒，皆养子傳國。

translations.literal: Later Yu also died of illness; both passed titles to adopted heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu died later; titles passed to adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 审忠字公诚，宦官诛后，辟公府。

translations.literal: Shen Zhong, courtesy name Gongcheng, after the eunuchs were purged was summoned to the Excellencies’ offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the massacre Shen Zhong entered grand secretary service.

sentences.zh: 吕强字汉盛，河南成皋人也。

translations.literal: Lü Qiang, courtesy name Hansheng, was a man of Chenggao in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qiang (courtesy Hansheng) came from Chenggao in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少以宦者为小黄門，再迁中常侍。

translations.literal: In youth he served as junior yellow gate and was twice promoted to regular palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from junior yellow gate to chief attendant.

sentences.zh: 为人清忠奉公。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure, loyal, and public-spirited.
translations.idiomatic: He was honest and devoted to the public good.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，例封宦者，以强为都乡侯。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ling the precedent enfeoffed eunuchs; Qiang was named marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling’s blanket enfeoffments made Lü Qiang a village marquis.

sentences.zh: 强辞让恳恻，固不敢当，帝乃聽之。

translations.literal: Qiang declined with earnest sincerity and firmly dared not accept; the emperor then listened.
translations.idiomatic: He tearfully refused until Lingdi relented.

sentences.zh: 因上疏陳事曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial stating affairs:
translations.idiomatic: His memorial opened with these arguments:

sentences.zh: 臣聞诸侯上象四七，下裂王土，高祖重约非功臣不侯，所以重天爵明劝戒也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the feudal lords above image the twenty-eight lodges and below divide the king’s soil; Gaozu stressed the covenant that none but merit-winners receive marquis rank—thereby honoring heaven’s nobility and clarifying encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Gaozu’s rule: nobility only for merit.

sentences.zh: 伏聞中常侍曹节、王甫、張让等，及侍中许相，并为列侯。

translations.literal: Your servant has learned that regular attendants Cao Jie, Wang Fu, Zhang Rang, and palace attendant Xu Xiang have together become full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He named Cao Jie, Wang Fu, Zhang Rang, and Xu Xiang as unworthy marquises.

sentences.zh: 节等宦官祐薄，品卑人贱，谗谄媚主，佞邪徼宠，放毒人物，疾妒忠良，有趙高之祸，未被轘裂之诛，掩朝廷之明，成私树之党。

translations.literal: Jie and other eunuchs enjoy thin fortune, low rank, and base persons; they slander and flatter the ruler, win favor through deceit, poison others, envy the loyal and good—they bear Zhao Gao’s guilt yet escaped being torn apart by carts; they obscure the court’s clarity and complete factions of private patronage.
