translations.idiomatic: These men were Zhao Gaos without the traitor’s fate—poisoning all beneath heaven’s clarity.

sentences.zh: 而陛下不悟，妄授茅土，开國承家，小人是用。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty has not awakened and rashly grants straw bundles and soil; founding states and continuing houses employs petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lingdi showered them with fiefs and emboldened petty men.

sentences.zh: 又并及家人，重金兼紫，相继为蕃辅。

translations.literal: Moreover reaching their households, heavy gold and purple sashes follow one another as assistants and guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Their kin wore purple and gold as ministers and tutors.

sentences.zh: 受國重恩，不念尔祖，述修厥德，而交结邪党，下比群佞。

translations.literal: Receiving the state’s deep favor, they do not recall their ancestors or cultivate virtue; instead they affiliate with wicked parties and sink to the level of the whole flock of flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: They dishonored imperial grace by building evil coalitions.

sentences.zh: 陛下或其琐才，特蒙恩泽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty perhaps regards their petty talents and specially showers grace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mistakes minor cleverness for worth.

sentences.zh: 又授位乖越，贤才不升，素餐私幸，必加荣擢。

translations.literal: Moreover appointments violate proper order: worthy talent does not advance while idle drones favored in private inevitably receive glory and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Meritless favorites leap ahead while worthies stall.

sentences.zh: 陰陽乖刺，稼穑荒蔬，人用不康，罔不由兹。

translations.literal: Yin and yang are out of joint; crops wither in wasteland; people lack peace—there is no cause but this.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth, harvests, and people suffer from these appointments alone.

sentences.zh: 臣诚知封事已行，言之无逮，所以冒死干触陳愚忠者，实愿陛下损改既谬，从此一止。

translations.literal: Your servant indeed knows the enfeoffments are already done and speech cannot catch them; the reason he risks death to offend with blunt loyalty is that he truly wishes Your Majesty to reduce and correct past errors and from this point halt.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing titles were already granted, he still begged Lingdi to stop the rot.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞后宫彩女数千余人，衣食之费，日数百余，比谷虽贱，而户有饥色。

translations.literal: Your servant further hears that the rear palace holds several thousand painted ladies whose clothing and food cost several hundred each day; though grain is cheap, every household shows famine in its face.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of harem women drained hundreds of cash daily while peasants starved.

sentences.zh: 案法当贵而今更贱者，由赋发繁数，以解县官，寒不敢衣，饥不敢食。

translations.literal: According to principle grain ought to be dear yet now is cheap because levies are frequent to supply the court treasury—people cold dare not clothe themselves, hungry dare not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Cheap grain masked ruinous taxes that left families unable to eat or dress.

sentences.zh: 民有斯厄，而莫之恤。

translations.literal: The people suffer this extremity yet none relieves them.
translations.idiomatic: No one pitied their plight.

sentences.zh: 宫女无用，填积后庭，天下虽复尽力耕桑，犹不能供。

translations.literal: Palace women serve no use yet pile up behind the rear halls; though the realm bends every effort to till and mulberry, it still cannot supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Useless concubines clogged the harem while farmers could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 昔楚女悲愁，則西官致灾，况终年积聚，岂无忧怨乎！

translations.literal: Formerly Chu women’s grief brought disaster on the western palace—how much more when they accumulate year after year can there fail to be resentment!
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Chu ladies’ sorrow fired omens; how much worse endless hoarding of girls?

sentences.zh: 夫天生蒸民，立君以牧之。

translations.literal: Heaven bore the teeming people and established a ruler to shepherd them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven made the people and set a ruler to tend them.

sentences.zh: 君道得，則民戴之如父母，仰之犹日月，虽時有征税，犹望其仁恩之惠。

translations.literal: When the ruler’s way is obtained the people cherish him as parents and look up to him like sun and moon; though levies come at times they still hope for kindness and grace.
translations.idiomatic: A true ruler wins love despite taxes.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：“悦以使民，民忘其劳；

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "With joy he employs the people and the people forget their toil;
translations.idiomatic: The Changes say delight makes people forget toil;

sentences.zh: 悦以犯难，民忘其死。

translations.literal: with joy he meets danger and the people forget death."
translations.idiomatic: delight in shared peril makes them forget death."

sentences.zh: ”储君副主，宜讽诵斯言；

translations.literal: The heir apparent and deputy lord ought to recite these words;
translations.idiomatic: The heir should memorize these lines;

sentences.zh: 南面当國，宜履行其事。

translations.literal: facing south to hold the state he ought to practice them in deed.
translations.idiomatic: the sovereign facing south must enact them.

sentences.zh: 又承詔書，当于河间故國起解渎之馆。

translations.literal: Moreover carrying out the edict to erect the Jiedu lodge on the old Hejian royal domain—
translations.idiomatic: He opposed building the Jiedu lodge at the old Hejian seat—

sentences.zh: 陛下龍飞即位，虽从籓國，然处九天之高，岂宜有顾恋之意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty soared aloft as dragon to the throne; though you came from a princedom, dwelling in the ninth heaven’s height, how should you cherish nostalgic longing?
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi had left his princedom for the throne—why cling to a provincial lodge?

sentences.zh: 且河间疏远，解渎邈绝，而当劳民单力，未见其便。

translations.literal: Moreover Hejian is remote and Jiedu far removed—to exhaust the people’s solitary strength brings no visible benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The project would waste the people for little gain.

sentences.zh: 又今外戚四姓贵幸之家，及中官公族无功德者，造起馆舍，凡有万数，楼阁连接，丹青素垩，雕刻之饰，不可单言。

translations.literal: Moreover the four houses of outer kindred enjoying favor and the eunuch public kindred without merit have raised lodges and halls numbering in the tens of thousands; belvederes link together with cinnabar, black, and white plaster and carving beyond brief description.
translations.idiomatic: Consort clans and sterile eunuch kin had thrown up countless mansions—balustrades, pigments, carvings beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 丧葬逾制，奢丽过礼，竞相放效，莫肯矫拂。

translations.literal: Funerals exceed regulation; extravagance surpasses ritual; they vie to imitate one another and none will correct excess.
translations.idiomatic: Burials exceeded sumptuary law in competitive luxury.

sentences.zh: 《穀梁傳》曰：“财尽則怨，力尽則怼。

translations.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: "When wealth is exhausted resentment arises; when strength is exhausted hatred arises."
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang warns: exhausting wealth breeds resentment; exhausting strength breeds rage.

sentences.zh: ”《尸子》曰：“君如杅，民如水，杅方則水方，杅圆則水圆。

translations.literal: The Master Shi says: "The ruler is like a pestle, the people like water—the pestle square then the water square; the pestle round then the water round."
translations.idiomatic: Shizi compares ruler to pestle and people to water—shape follows shape.

sentences.zh: ”上之化下，犹风之靡草。

translations.literal: What is above transforms what is below like wind bending grass.
translations.idiomatic: The throne bends folkways as wind bends grass.

sentences.zh: 今上无去奢之俭，下有纵欲之敝，至使禽兽食民之甘，木土衣民之帛。

translations.literal: Now above there is no austerity casting off extravagance; below runs the ruin of indulged desires—so that beasts and birds eat the sweetness owed to the people, and timber and rammed earth wear the silks owed to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Above there is no restraint of luxury; below desire runs riot until birds and beasts feast on food meant for peasants and halls wear silk meant for men.

sentences.zh: 昔师旷谏晋平公曰：“梁柱衣绣，民无褐衣；

translations.literal: Formerly Shi Kuang remonstrated with Duke Ping of Jin: "When pillars and beams wear embroidery, the common people lack coarse cloth;
translations.idiomatic: Music master Shi Kuang warned Duke Ping of Jin: when palace beams are brocaded, commoners lack hemp—

sentences.zh: 池有弃酒，士有渴死；

translations.literal: when pools hold discarded wine, gentlemen die of thirst;
translations.idiomatic: wine pools overflow while scholars thirst—

sentences.zh: 厩馬秣粟，民有饥色。

translations.literal: when stable horses feed on grain, the people show famine in their faces.
translations.idiomatic: stable horses eat grain while peasants starve.

sentences.zh: 近臣不敢谏，远臣不得暢。

translations.literal: Close ministers dare not remonstrate; distant ministers cannot get their words through."
translations.idiomatic: Inner courtiers dare not speak; outer officials cannot be heard."

sentences.zh: ”此之谓也。

translations.literal: This is what was meant.
translations.idiomatic: That is the warning he meant.

sentences.zh: 又聞前召议郎蔡邕对问于金商門，而令中常侍曹节、王甫等以詔書喻旨。

translations.literal: Your servant further hears that previously Gentleman for Discussion Cai Yong was summoned for questioning at the Golden Merchant Gate while regular attendants Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and others conveyed edict intent.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong was questioned at Golden Merchant Gate while Cao Jie and Wang Fu relayed the emperor’s scripted prompts.

sentences.zh: 邕不敢怀道迷國，而切言极对，毁刺贵臣，讥呵竖宦。

translations.literal: Yong did not dare harbor the Way yet betray the state; he spoke bluntly with utmost replies, attacking noble ministers and ridiculing the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong answered bluntly, attacking grandees and mocking the inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 陛下不密其言，至令宣露，群邪项领，膏脣拭舌，竞欲咀嚼，造作飞条。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty did not keep his words secret until they leaked; throngs of villains crane their necks, grease their lips and wipe their tongues, each eager to chew him over and spin flying accusations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaked his answers; sycophants smeared him with rumors.

sentences.zh: 陛下回受诽谤，致邕刑罪，室家徙放，老幼流离，岂不负忠臣哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty turned and swallowed slander, subjected Yong to punishment and crime, banished his household, old and young adrift in exile—how is this not betraying a loyal subject!
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi believed libel, punished Cai Yong, and scattered his family—hardly the reward of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今群臣皆以邕为戒，上畏不测之难，下惧剑客之害，臣知朝廷不复得聞忠言矣。

translations.literal: Now every minister takes Yong as a warning—above fearing unforeseen calamity, below fearing assassins—your servant knows the court will never again hear loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Officials now stay silent, fearing jail or knives—no one will speak truth again.

sentences.zh: 故太尉段熲，武勇冠世，习于边事，垂发服戎，功成皓首，历事二主，勋烈独昭。

translations.literal: Thus former Grand Commandant Duan Jiong: martial courage foremost in his age, practiced in frontier affairs; from youth he served in arms until white-haired with merit, serving two sovereigns—his merit-blaze uniquely clear.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong had spent a lifetime on the frontier for two emperors with shining merit.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已式序，位登台司，而为司隶校尉陽球所见诬胁，一身既毙，而妻子远播。

translations.literal: Your Majesty had already ranked him in order and promoted him to the Three Excellencies, yet he was slandered and coerced by Metropolitan Superintendent Yang Qiu—his person perished and wife and children were cast far away.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to the summit, he fell to Yang Qiu’s frame-up and died; his family was exiled.

sentences.zh: 天下惆怅，功臣失望。

translations.literal: All under heaven were aggrieved; meritorious servants despaired.
translations.idiomatic: The empire grieved; veterans lost heart.

sentences.zh: 宜征邕更授任， 反颎家属，則忠卢路开，众怨以弭矣。

translations.literal: It would be fitting to summon Yong for renewed appointment and restore Jiong’s family—then roads for loyalty open and popular resentment may be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: Recall Cai Yong and restore Duan Jiong’s kin to clear the path for loyal service.

sentences.zh: 帝知其忠而不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Qiang was loyal yet could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling knew Lü Qiang was honest but ignored him.

sentences.zh: 時，帝多稸私臧，收天下之珍，每郡國贡献，先输中署，名为“导行费”。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor stored much private treasure, gathered the realm’s rarities; whenever commanderies and kingdoms offered tribute it first went to the inner workshops under the name "conduit travel fee."
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi hoarded tribute in private vaults, skimming “guide fees” before state receipt.

sentences.zh: 强上疏谏曰：

translations.literal: Qiang submitted a memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qiang memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 天下之财，莫不生之陰陽，归之陛下。

translations.literal: Wealth under heaven is born of yin and yang and returns to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: All wealth ultimately belongs to the throne.

sentences.zh: 归之陛下，岂有公私？

translations.literal: Once it returns to Your Majesty, how can there be public versus private?
translations.idiomatic: In your hands it cannot be split into private hoards and public funds.

sentences.zh: 而今中尚方敛诸郡之宝，中御府积天下之缯，西园引司农之臧，中厩聚太仆之馬，而所输之府，辄有导行之财。

translations.literal: Yet now the Inner Imperial Workshop gathers treasures from commanderies, the Inner Treasury piles silks from the realm, the Western Garden draws from the minister of agriculture’s stores, the Inner Stables cluster the minister of horses’ mounts—and whatever office receives tribute still pays conduit fees.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Inner Workshops, Inner Treasury, Western Garden, and imperial stables stockpiled gifts while every delivery paid squeeze money.

sentences.zh: 调广民困，费多献少，奸吏因其利，百姓受其敝。

translations.literal: Levies spread wide while the people suffer; expenses rise though offerings shrink; corrupt clerks profit and commoners bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wide levies impoverished the people; clerks skimmed while peasants broke.

sentences.zh: 又阿媚之臣，好献其私，容谄姑息，自此而进。

translations.literal: Moreover fawning ministers gladly offer their private goods; tolerance and flattery advance thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophants greased the system with private kickbacks.

sentences.zh: 旧典选举委任三府，三府有选，参议掾属，咨其行状，度其器能，受试任用，责以成功。

translations.literal: By ancient statute selection was entrusted to the Three Excellencies; when the Three Excellencies had candidates, aides deliberated, consulted conduct records, assessed capacity, tested appointment, and demanded success.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Three Excellencies vetted candidates through their staffs—

sentences.zh: 若无可察，然后付之尚書。

translations.literal: If nothing needed inspection, only then was it handed to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: only then did cases reach the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尚書举劾，请下廷尉，覆案虚实，行其诛罚。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing impeached, requested referral to the commandant of justice, reviewed truth and falsehood, and carried out execution and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing impeached offenders, sent cases to the commandant of justice for review, verified guilt, and carried out sentences.

sentences.zh: 今但任尚書，或复敕用。

translations.literal: Now appointment rests solely with the Masters of Writing or ad hoc edict.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lingdi bypassed the Excellencies and appointed by edict alone.

sentences.zh: 如是，三公得免选举之负，尚書亦复不坐，责赏无归，岂肯空自苦劳乎！

translations.literal: In such fashion the Three Excellencies escape responsibility for selection, the Masters of Writing likewise bear no blame—reward and blame attach nowhere; who would willingly labor for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Excellencies and Masters of Writing both escaped blame—so neither bothered to vet appointees.

sentences.zh: 夫立言无显过之咎，明镜无见玼之尤。

translations.literal: Setting forth words brings no manifest fault; a bright mirror bears no blame for showing blemish.
translations.idiomatic: Honest counsel risks no crime; mirrors do not sin by revealing flaws.

sentences.zh: 如恶立言以记过，則不当學也；

translations.literal: If you hate words that record faults then one ought not study;
translations.idiomatic: If you forbid criticism you forbid learning—

sentences.zh: 不欲明镜之见玼，則不当照也。

translations.literal: if you do not wish a bright mirror to show blemish then one ought not look into it.
translations.idiomatic: if you ban mirrors you ban self-knowledge.

sentences.zh: 愿陛下详思臣言，不以记过见玼为责。

translations.literal: Your servant begs Your Majesty to ponder his words carefully and not reproach record of faults or showing of blemish.
translations.idiomatic: He begged Lingdi not to punish candor as treason.

sentences.zh: 書奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted without imperial review.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ignored it.

sentences.zh: 中平元年，黄巾贼起，帝问强所宜施行。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongping (184) the Yellow Turban rebels arose; the emperor asked Qiang what ought to be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans rose, Lingdi asked Lü Qiang’s advice.

sentences.zh: 强欲先诛左右贪浊者，大赦党人，料简刺史、二千石能否。

translations.literal: Qiang wished first to execute the greedy and corrupt around the throne, grant great amnesty to "faction" victims, and assess whether inspectors and two-thousand-shi officials were competent.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qiang urged executing corrupt eunuchs, amnestying the faction purge victims, and auditing regional governors.

sentences.zh: 帝纳之，乃先赦党人。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it and first amnestied the faction members.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi first freed the purged scholars.

sentences.zh: 于是诸常侍人人求退，又各自征还宗亲子弟在州郡者。

translations.literal: Thereupon every regular attendant begged to retire and each recalled adoptive sons and blood relatives serving in commanderies and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chief eunuchs feigned retreat and recalled kin from local posts.

sentences.zh: 中常侍趙忠、夏恽等遂共构强，云“与党人共议朝廷，数读《霍光傳》。

translations.literal: Regular attendants Zhao Zhong, Xia Yun, and others together framed Qiang, saying "He plots with faction men about court affairs and repeatedly reads the biography of Huo Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhong and Xia Yun accused Lü Qiang of faction plots and reading Huo Guang’s biography—

sentences.zh: 强兄弟所在并皆贪秽”。

translations.literal: "Qiang’s brothers wherever stationed are all greedy and filthy."
translations.idiomatic: claiming his brothers were corrupt everywhere.

sentences.zh: 帝不悦，使中黄門持兵召强。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and sent central yellow gates with weapons to summon Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: An angry emperor summoned Lü Qiang under arms.

sentences.zh: 强聞帝召，怒曰：“吾死，乱起矣。

translations.literal: When Qiang heard the summons he angrily said: "When I die rebellion will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qiang cried, "My death marks the coming chaos."

sentences.zh: 丈夫欲尽忠國家，岂能对狱吏乎！

translations.literal: A man who wishes to exhaust loyalty to the state—how can he answer to prison clerks!"
translations.idiomatic: A patriot does not submit to jailers!"

sentences.zh: ”遂自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He killed himself.

sentences.zh: 忠、恽复谮曰：“强见召未知所问，而就处草自屏，有奸明审。

translations.literal: Zhong and Yun slandered further: "When Qiang was summoned without knowing the charge he hastened to kill himself beside grass—his guilt is obvious."
translations.idiomatic: They claimed suicide proved guilt.

sentences.zh: ”遂收捕宗亲，没入财产焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they arrested his kin and confiscated property.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was seized and assets forfeited.

sentences.zh: 時，宦者济陰丁肃、下邳徐衍、南陽郭耽、汝陽李巡、北海趙祐等五人称为清忠，皆在里巷，不争威权。

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs Ding Su of Jiyin, Xu Yan of Xiapi, Guo Dan of Nanyang, Li Xun of Ruyang, and Zhao You of Beihai—five men—were deemed pure and loyal; all kept to their lanes and did not contend for power.
translations.idiomatic: Five eunuchs—Ding Su, Xu Yan, Guo Dan, Li Xun, Zhao You—were praised as honest and stayed clear of power struggles.

sentences.zh: 巡以为诸博士试甲乙科，争弟高下，更相告言，至有行赂定兰台漆書經字，以合其私文者，乃白帝，与诸儒共刻《五經》文于石，于是詔蔡邕等正其文字。

translations.literal: Xun believed that when erudites tested Class A and B the wrangling over rank led to mutual accusations, even to bribing to alter lacquer-book classics on the Orchid Terrace to match private texts; he therefore reported to the emperor and with various scholars carved the Five Classics text in stone, whereupon an edict ordered Cai Yong and others to rectify the graphs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun ended canon disputes by proposing the stone classics with Cai Yong correcting the text.

sentences.zh: 自后《五經》一定，争者用息。

translations.literal: Afterward the Five Classics were fixed and wrangling ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The stone steles settled the text and ended wrangling.

sentences.zh: 趙祐博學多览，著作校書，诸儒称之。

translations.literal: Zhao You was broadly learned, compiled and collated books, and the scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You edited palace texts to scholarly acclaim.

sentences.zh: 又小黄門甘陵吴伉，善为风角，博达有奉公称。

translations.literal: Moreover junior yellow gate Wu Kang of Ganling was skilled in wind-angle divination and broadly learned, with a reputation for public integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kang of Ganling practiced wind-angle astrology and public service.

sentences.zh: 知不得用，常托病还寺舍，从容养志云。

translations.literal: Knowing he would not be employed, he often pleaded illness and returned to his lodge, leisurely nurturing his will, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no use for his counsel he lived in reclusive illness.

sentences.zh: 張让、趙忠

translations.literal: Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong—

sentences.zh: 張让者，颎川人；

translations.literal: Zhang Rang was a man of Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang came from Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 趙忠者，安平人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhong was a man of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhong from Anping.

sentences.zh: 少皆给事者中，桓帝時为小黄門。

translations.literal: In youth both served in the palace; under Emperor Huan they were junior yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: They entered palace service young and became junior yellow gates under Huan.

sentences.zh: 忠以与诛梁冀功封都乡侯。

translations.literal: Zhong was enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang for merit in executing Liang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhong earned a village marquisate in the Liang Ji coup.

sentences.zh: 延熹八年，黜为关内侯，食本县租千斛。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yanxi he was degraded to secondary marquis drawing one thousand hu rent from his native county.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 165 he fell to secondary marquis on one thousand hu local rent.

sentences.zh: 斋

translations.literal: Erratum.
translations.idiomatic: Scribal slip.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，让、忠并迁中常侍，封列侯，与曹节、王甫等相为表里。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ling Rang and Zhong were together promoted to regular palace attendants, enfeoffed as full marquises, and acted in mutual cover with Cao Jie and Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ling they rose to chief attendants and full marquises in league with Cao Jie and Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 节死后，忠领大长秋。

translations.literal: After Jie died Zhong headed grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Jie died Zhao Zhong became grand prolonger of autumn.

sentences.zh: 让有监奴典任家事，交通货赂，威形喧赫。

translations.literal: Rang had a steward slave managing household affairs who trafficked in bribes—his awe-inspiring presence was notorious.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang’s majordomo traded favors and terrified Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 扶风人孟佗，资产饶赡，与奴朋结，倾谒馈问，无所遗爱。

translations.literal: Meng Tuo of Fufeng, richly endowed, befriended the slave with visits and gifts withholding nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy Meng Tuo bribed that slave lavishly.

sentences.zh: 奴咸德之，问佗曰：“君何所欲？

translations.literal: The slaves all thanked him and asked: "What do you desire?
translations.idiomatic: The slaves asked what reward he wanted—

sentences.zh: 力能办也。

translations.literal: Our strength can accomplish it."
translations.idiomatic: "We can deliver anything."

sentences.zh: ”曰：“吾望汝曹为我一拜耳。

translations.literal: He said: "I only wish you would bow once for me."
translations.idiomatic: He asked only for one ceremonial bow.

sentences.zh: ”時宾客求谒让者，車恒数百千两，佗時指让，后至，不得进，监奴乃率诸仓头迎拜于路，遂共轝車入門。

translations.literal: At that time guests seeking audience with Rang numbered hundreds or thousands of carriages; when Tuo went to see Rang he arrived late and could not enter, but the steward led all the warehouse slaves to bow to him on the road and together hoisted the carriage through the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng arrived late to Zhang Rang’s jammed gate, the majordomo had grooms prostrate and carry his cart inside—

sentences.zh: 宾客咸惊，谓佗善于让，皆争以珍玩赂之。

translations.literal: Guests were all astonished, thinking Tuo was on good terms with Rang, and vied to bribe him with treasures.
translations.idiomatic: guests assumed Meng was Zhang’s intimate and showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 佗分以遗让，让大喜，遂以佗为凉州刺史。

translations.literal: Tuo divided gifts to present to Rang; Rang was greatly pleased and thereupon made Tuo inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Meng split the loot with Zhang Rang and bought the Liang Province inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 是時，让、忠及夏恽、郭胜、孙璋、毕岚、栗嵩、段珪、高望、張恭、韩悝、宋典十二人，皆为中常侍，封侯贵宠，父兄子弟布列州郡，所在贪贱，为人蠹害。

translations.literal: At this time Rang, Zhong together with Xia Yun, Guo Sheng, Sun Zhang, Bi Lan, Li Song, Duan Gui, Gao Wang, Zhang Gong, Han Kui, Song Dian—twelve men in all—were all regular palace attendants, enfeoffed and favored; fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews filled prefectures and commanderies, everywhere greedy and base, harming the people like worms.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve chief eunuchs—including Zhang, Zhao, Xia Yun, and Duan Gui—lorded over the provinces through corrupt kin.

sentences.zh: 黄巾既作，盗贼糜沸，郎中中山張钧上書曰：“窃惟張角所以能兴兵作乱，万人所以乐附之者，其源皆由十常侍多放父兄、子弟、婚亲、宾客典据州郡，辜榷财利，侵掠百姓，百姓之冤无所告诉，故谋议不轨，聚为盗贼。

translations.literal: After the Yellow Turbans arose bandits boiled like porridge; Palace Gentleman Zhang Jun of Zhongshan submitted a memorial: "Your servant privately considers that the reason Zhang Jue could raise troops and rebel and ten thousand men gladly attached themselves is that their source lies entirely in the ten regular attendants placing fathers, elder brothers, sons, nephews, marriage kin, and guests to hold commanderies and prefectures, monopolizing profit and plundering commoners—common people’s wrongs have nowhere to appeal, therefore they plot rebellion and gather as bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun traced the rebellion to eunuch kin looting the provinces.

sentences.zh: 宜斩十常侍，县头南郊，以谢百姓，又遣使者布告天下，可不须师旅，而大寇自消。

translations.literal: It would be fitting to behead the ten regular attendants, hang their heads at the southern suburb to apologize to the people, moreover dispatch envoys to proclaim throughout the realm—then without mobilizing troops the great robbers will vanish of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Behead the Ten Attendants and hang them south of the city—no army needed.

sentences.zh: ”天子以钧章示让等，皆免冠徒跣顿首，乞自致洛陽詔狱，并出家财以助军费。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven showed Rang and others Jun’s memorial; all doffed caps, went barefoot, and knocked their heads begging to surrender themselves to Luoyang imperial prison and moreover donate household wealth to aid military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi showed the memorial; the eunuchs knelt barefoot offering prison and cash.

sentences.zh: 有詔皆冠履视事如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them all to resume caps, shoes, and duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Edict refused—they kept their posts.

sentences.zh: 帝怒钧曰：“此真狂子也。

translations.literal: The emperor raged at Jun: "This is truly a madman.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi roared that Zhang Jun was insane.

sentences.zh: 十常侍固当有一人善者不？

translations.literal: Among the ten regular attendants surely there must be one who is good?"
translations.idiomatic: "Surely one of the Ten is decent?"

sentences.zh: ”钧复重上，犹如前章，辄寝不报。

translations.literal: Jun submitted again heavily, still like his previous memorial—it was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun repeated his plea; it sank without trace.

sentences.zh: 詔使廷尉、侍御史考为張角道者，御史承让等旨，遂诬奏钧學黄巾道，收掠死狱中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the commandant of justice and attendant clerk to examine those who practiced Zhang Jue’s Way; the clerk, obeying Rang and others’ intent, falsely memorialized that Jun studied Yellow Turban doctrine, seized and tortured him to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Courts framed Zhang Jun as a Yellow Turban and killed him in jail.

sentences.zh: 而让等实多与張角交通。

translations.literal: Yet Rang and others in truth had much traffic with Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Rang secretly dealt with Zhang Jue.

sentences.zh: 后中常侍封谞、徐奉事独发觉坐诛，帝因怒诘让等曰：“汝曹常言党人欲为不轨，皆令禁锢，或有伏诛。

translations.literal: Later regular attendant Feng Xu and Xu Feng alone had their dealings exposed and were executed; the emperor thereupon angrily questioned Rang and others: "You lot always say faction men plot rebellion and all should be confined or executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Xu fell, Lingdi demanded why eunuchs consorted with rebels after scholars were purged.

sentences.zh: 今党人更为國用，汝曹反与張角通，为可斩未？

translations.literal: Now faction men again serve the state while you lot instead communicate with Zhang Jue—should you be beheaded or not?"
translations.idiomatic: "Scholars serve you again while you traffic with Zhang Jue—should you die?"

sentences.zh: ”皆叩头云：“故中常侍王甫、侯览所为。

translations.literal: All knocked their heads saying: "It was what former regular attendant Wang Fu and Hou Lan did."
translations.idiomatic: They blamed the dead Wang Fu and Hou Lan.

sentences.zh: ”帝乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi let it drop.

sentences.zh: 明年，南宫灾。

translations.literal: The next year the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Southern Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 让、忠等说帝令敛天下田亩税十钱，以修宫室。

translations.literal: Rang, Zhong, and others persuaded the emperor to levy ten cash per field of farmland across the realm to repair palace buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang taxed every mou ten coins to rebuild.

sentences.zh: 发太原、河东、狄道诸郡材木及文石，每州郡部送至京师，黄門常侍辄令谴呵不中者，因强折贱买，十分雇一，因复货之于宦官，复不为即受，材木遂至腐积，宫室连年不成。

translations.literal: Timber from Taiyuan, Hedong, Didao commanderies and patterned stone were dispatched from each prefecture to the capital; yellow gates and regular attendants invariably abused and rejected loads that did not suit them, forcibly broke prices to buy cheap—one tenth of hire—and resold to eunuchs; again they delayed acceptance so timber rotted piled up and palace construction remained unfinished year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Regional lumber rotted on docks while eunuchs haggled and resold bribes.

sentences.zh: 刺史、太守复增私调，百姓呼嗟。

translations.literal: Inspectors and prefects added private levies; common people wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Governors added surcharges; people howled.

sentences.zh: 凡詔所征求，皆令西园驺密约敕，号曰“中使”，恐动州郡，多受赇赂。

translations.literal: Whatever edicts demanded west-garden grooms made secret bargains—styled "palace envoys"—terrorizing commanderies and prefectures and taking many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Western Garden brokers shook down provinces as “palace envoys.”

sentences.zh: 刺史、二千石及茂才孝廉迁除，皆责助军修宫钱，大郡至二三千万，余各有差。

translations.literal: Inspectors, two-thousand-shi officials, and candidates elevated as abundance talent or filial integrity for promotion all paid military-support palace-repair cash—great commanderies up to twenty or thirty million, the rest in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: every promotion required “army and palace” payments—millions for large commanderies.

sentences.zh: 当之官者，皆先至西园谐价，然后得去。

translations.literal: Those about to take office all first went to the Western Garden to haggle price, then could depart.
translations.idiomatic: New officials bid for posts at Western Garden before leaving.

sentences.zh: 有钱不毕者，或至自殺。

translations.literal: Those without enough cash sometimes committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Some killed themselves over unpaid fees.

sentences.zh: 其守清者，乞不之官，皆迫遣之。

translations.literal: Those who kept pure begged not to take office yet were forced to go.
translations.idiomatic: Honest men who refused were driven to post anyway.

sentences.zh: 時，钜鹿太守河内司馬直新除，以有清名，减责三百万。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Administrator of Julu Sima Zhi of Henei had newly received appointment; because he had a reputation for purity his assessed fee was reduced three million.
translations.idiomatic: Julu’s new governor Sima Zhi, famed as honest, owed only three million cash.

sentences.zh: 直被詔，帐然曰：“为民父母，而反割剥百姓，以称時求，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict he sighed in dismay: "As father and mother to the people yet turning to strip the common people to meet timely demands—I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi said parents of the people should not skin the people for politics.

sentences.zh: ”辞疾，不聽，行至孟津，上書极陳当世之失，古今祸败之戒，即吞药自殺。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness but was not permitted; proceeding as far as Mengjin he submitted a memorial exhaustively stating contemporary failures and lessons of ancient calamity, then swallowed poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Denied sick leave, he memorialized at Mengjin and took poison.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝为暂绝修宫钱。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented the emperor for the moment suspended palace-repair cash.
translations.idiomatic: His death briefly halted the palace levy.

sentences.zh: 又造万金堂于西园，引司农金钱缯帛，仞积其中。

translations.literal: Moreover he built the Hall of Myriad Gold in the Western Garden, drawing minister of agriculture cash, silks, and brocade to pile therein.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi piled treasury silver in the Hall of Myriad Gold.

sentences.zh: 又还河间买田宅，起第观。

translations.literal: Moreover he returned to Hejian to buy fields and residences and raise mansions and belvederes.
translations.idiomatic: He bought estates in Hejian and built towers.

sentences.zh: 帝本侯家，宿贫，每叹桓帝不能作家居，故聚为私臧，复寄小黄門常侍钱各数千万。

translations.literal: The emperor came from a marquis family and long been poor; he often sighed that Emperor Huan could not build a household estate, therefore amassed private stores and moreover deposited several tens of millions with junior yellow gates and regular attendants.
translations.idiomatic: A former poor marquis, Ling envied Huan’s wealth and stashed millions with eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 常云：“張常侍是我公，趙常侍是我母。

translations.literal: He often said: "Regular attendant Zhang is my father; regular attendant Zhao is my mother."
translations.idiomatic: He called Zhang Rang “father” and Zhao Zhong “mother.”

sentences.zh: ”宦者得志，无所惮畏，并起第宅，拟則宫室。

translations.literal: The eunuchs having gained their will feared nothing, together raised mansions rivaling palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, they built palaces for themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝常登永安候台，宦官恐其望见居外，乃使中大人尚但谏曰：“天子不当登高，登高則百姓虚散。

translations.literal: The emperor often climbed the Yong’an marquis terrace; the eunuchs feared he might gaze upon dwellings outside and therefore sent palace attendant Shang Dan to remonstrate: "The Son of Heaven ought not ascend to heights; ascending heights causes the common people to scatter like emptiness."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling liked to mount the Yong’an belvedere; eunuchs feared he might see mansions beyond the palace and sent Shang Dan to warn him that an emperor should not climb high—looking outward would “scatter” the people.
(Manuscript punctuation fragment joined to preceding quotation.)

sentences.zh: ”自是不敢复升台榭。

translations.literal: Thereafter he did not dare climb terraces again.
translations.idiomatic: After that he never climbed another tower.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂使钩盾令宋典缮修南宫玉堂。

translations.literal: The next year he ordered Vault Shield superintendent Song Dian to repair the Jade Hall of the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He put Song Dian in charge of rebuilding the Southern Palace Jade Hall.

sentences.zh: 又使掖庭令毕岚铸铜人四列于仓龍、玄武阙，又铸四钟，皆受二千斛，县于玉堂及云台殿前。

translations.literal: He also ordered Rear Palace superintendent Bi Lan to cast four bronze statues in rows at Canglong and Xuanwu gates, and cast four bells each holding two thousand hu, hung before the Jade Hall and Cloud Terrace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Lan cast four giant bronze figures at the Canglong and Xuanwu towers and four bells of two thousand hu each for the Jade Hall and Cloud Terrace.

sentences.zh: 又铸天禄虾蟆，吐水于平門外桥东，转水入宫。

translations.literal: Moreover he cast celestial deer and giant toads spitting water east of the bridge outside Ping Gate to turn water into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He added bronze waterworks east of Ping Gate to pump river water inward.

sentences.zh: 又作翻車渴乌，旋于桥西，用洒南北郊路，以省百姓洒道之费。

translations.literal: Moreover he made chain pumps and “thirsty crows” west of the bridge to sprinkle the roads to the southern and northern suburbs and spare common people the expense of sprinkling the roads.
translations.idiomatic: West of the bridge he installed pumps and siphons to sprinkle suburban roads at state expense.

sentences.zh: 又铸四出文钱，钱皆四道。

translations.literal: Moreover he cast cash with four raised rims—every coin bore four ridges.
translations.idiomatic: He minted “four-spoke” coins with raised edges in four directions.

sentences.zh: 识者窃言侈虐已甚，形象兆见，此钱成，必四道而去。

translations.literal: Those with discernment whispered that extravagance had reached its limit and omens had appeared in images—once this cash was finished it would surely “go out four ways.”
translations.idiomatic: Critics said the coin’s four ridges foretold the realm splitting four ways.

sentences.zh: 及京师大乱，钱果流布四海。

translations.literal: When great chaos struck the capital the coin indeed circulated throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell the debased coin spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 复以忠为車骑将军，百余日罢。

translations.literal: Again Zhao Zhong was made general of chariots and cavalry and after a hundred-odd days was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhong briefly held general of chariots and cavalry, then lost it within months.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Emperor Ling died.

sentences.zh: 中军校尉袁绍说大将军何进，令诛中官以悦天下。

translations.literal: Colonel of the central army Yuan Shao persuaded Grand General He Jin to execute the inner attendants to please the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao urged He Jin to slaughter the eunuchs to win the empire.

sentences.zh: 谋泄，让、忠等因进入省，遂共殺进。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; Rang, Zhong, and others therefore entered the palace precincts and together killed Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The plan leaked; Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong ambushed He Jin inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 而绍勒兵斩忠，捕宦官无少长悉斩之。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan Shao led troops, beheaded Zhong, and arrested eunuchs without sparing age—executing all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao then slaughtered every eunuch in Luoyang, young or old.

sentences.zh: 让等数十人劫质天子走河上。

translations.literal: Rang and several dozen others seized the Son of Heaven as hostage and fled toward the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang fled north holding the boy emperor hostage.

sentences.zh: 追急，让等悲哭辞曰：“臣等殄灭，天下乱矣。

translations.literal: Pressed hard, Rang and the others wept in farewell: "When your servants are extinguished the realm will fall into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Zhang Rang cried, "When we die the realm collapses."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下自爱！

translations.literal: Only hope Your Majesty cherishes himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Only preserve yourself, Majesty!"

sentences.zh: ”皆投河而死。

translations.literal: All threw themselves into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: They leaped into the Yellow River and drowned.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古丧大业绝宗禋者，其所渐有由矣。

translations.literal: Appended judgment: From antiquity those who lost great enterprises and cut off ancestral sacrifice—the gradual causes have their origins.
translations.idiomatic: The historian reflects: dynastic ruin always grows from slow causes.

sentences.zh: 三代以嬖色取祸，嬴氏以奢虐致灾，西京自外戚失祚，东都缘阉尹倾國。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties suffered calamity through favored beauties; the House of Ying brought disaster through extravagance and cruelty; Western Capital lost the mandate through maternal kin; Eastern Capital overturned the state through chief eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Xia-Shang-Zhou fell to palace women; Qin to cruelty; Chang’an to consort clans; Luoyang to eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 成败之來，先史商之久矣。

translations.literal: Victory and defeat’s arrival—the earlier histories long debated it.
translations.idiomatic: Historians have quarreled over these patterns for ages.

sentences.zh: 至于衅起宦夫，其略犹或可言。

translations.literal: As for disaster arising from eunuchs, its outline may still be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch catastrophe can still be traced in outline.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 刑余之丑，理谢全生，声荣无辉于門阀，肌肤莫傳于來体，推情未鉴其敝，即事易以取信，加渐染朝事，颇识典物，故少主凭谨旧之庸，女君资出内之命，顾访无猜惮之心，恩狎有可悦之色。

translations.literal: The disgrace of mutilated punishment cuts them off from intact life; glory and honor cast no radiance on their gates; flesh cannot pass to posterity—extend sympathy and one misses their vice; judge present deeds and they easily win trust; steeped in court affairs they master precedent and ritual; hence young rulers rely on their diligent convention, female sovereigns borrow their commands for inner and outer traffic—personal audiences harbor no suspicion, intimate favor presents pleasing colors.
translations.idiomatic: Castrates lack heirs yet live inside the palace—juvenile empresses and boy emperors trust their daily companions who know palace routine better than ministers.

sentences.zh: 亦有忠厚平端，怀术纠邪；

translations.literal: Some are loyal, thick, even-handed, harboring arts to correct evil;
translations.idiomatic: Some served faithfully or corrected abuses—

sentences.zh: 或敏才给对，饰巧乱实；

translations.literal: others quick at repartee ornament craft and confuse truth;
translations.idiomatic: others masked poison with wit—

sentences.zh: 或借誉贞良，先時荐誉。

translations.literal: others borrow reputation for integrity and recommend worthies ahead of time.
translations.idiomatic: others bought virtue by sponsoring scholars early.

sentences.zh: 非直苟恣凶德，止于暴横而已。

translations.literal: Not merely indulging vicious conduct stopping at violence and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Their evil was not only crude bullying.

sentences.zh: 然莫邪并行，情貌相越，故能回惑昏幼，迷瞀视聽，盖亦有其理焉。

translations.literal: Yet true and false ran parallel; inner feeling and outer face diverged—therefore they could turn confusion in dim-witted youth, blind sight and hearing; indeed they had their rationale.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicity let them deceive child emperors while seeming indispensable.

sentences.zh: 诈利既滋，朋徒日广，直臣抗议，必漏先言之间，至戚发愤，方启专夺之隙，斯忠贤所以智屈，社稷故其为墟。

translations.literal: Once fraud’s profit swelled, partisans daily widened; upright ministers who protested saw words leak beforehand through informers; close kin who roused rage opened gaps for sole seizure—this is why loyal worthies found wisdom exhausted and why altars became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Honest officials were betrayed before they acted; kin of the throne moved too late—so wise men failed and the state fell.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：“履霜坚冰至。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Treading on frost, hard ice arrives."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes warn: tread frost and solid ice follows.

sentences.zh: ”云所从來久矣。

translations.literal: It means what comes has been long in coming.
translations.idiomatic: The saying marks how long rot had been building.

sentences.zh: 今迹其所以，亦岂一朝一夕哉！

translations.literal: Now tracing how it happened—how could it have been a single morning or evening!
translations.idiomatic: Tracing these causes shows no sudden overnight collapse.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：“任失无小，过用則违。

translations.literal: Encomium says: "When appointment misses its mark there is no fault too small; excess use brings rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The closing hymn begins: no mis-appointment is too small to matter—push favor too far and it turns traitor.

sentences.zh: 况乃巷职，远参天机。

translations.literal: How much more alley offices reaching far into heaven’s secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Still worse when lane-born stewards reach into the throne’s innermost secrets.

sentences.zh: 舞文巧态，作惠作威。

translations.literal: Twisting documents and crafty postures—they dispense kindness and wield dread.
translations.idiomatic: They twist writs and strike clever poses, playing benefactor today and executioner tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 凶家害國，夫岂异归！

translations.literal: Ruining houses and harming the state—does the outcome differ!
translations.idiomatic: They destroy clans and kingdoms alike—the ruin always rhymes."
